segmentation.text: Upon approaching an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Be prepared to stop.

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'an authorized emergency vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'), claimed as ru.aggregate; its 'not a stand-in for' a responding role does not bite, since the conduct the words require of it (lights in use, motion) is read separately. 'an official vehicle of a regulatory agency' is ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency ('a vehicle in official or contracted road service ... kind ∈ {..., regulatory_agency, ...}'), not read as an emergency vehicle. 'Upon approaching': the subject, moving (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', above the halt tolerance), has that vehicle ahead of it (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component positive) within the approach reach of centre distance (rel.centre_distance, 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points'; no clearance or order of arrival is read from it). 'which is moving': the vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance. 'or preparing to move', as the section defines it (s8): the vehicle visible from the subject (rel.visible, 'an unobstructed line of sight from a's reference point to b's body'; not a distance, not a lit lamp) showing an arm signal (sig.hand_signal meaning other than no_signal) or a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator left or right: the signal, not the manoeuvre). 'in any direction' adds no restriction: no heading of the vehicle is read. The vehicle is quantified in the formula, never a binder.

sig.warning_lamp: 'a warning lamp lit; colour ∈ {red, blue, amber, white}, mode ∈ {flashing, rotating, steady}, facing ∈ {front, rear, side}'. The words borrowed from DEF-NRS-484A-480-3, 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front', fix which lights meet the requirements: a lamp lit on the approached vehicle of colour red, mode flashing, facing front. Not a stand-in for an audible warning: no siren is read, the words name lights only.

'any other vehicle' is the defined term vehicle, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); its exclusions (devices moved by human power, electric bicycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices, electric scooters) are the reading's classification under that id, never expanded here. 'other' excludes the approached vehicle: the subject and it are not the same road user. 'the driver' is a relational role, not an aggregate: read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

dev.human_direction: 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}': a law enforcement officer is role police_officer, the other roles are not law enforcement officers. The exception holds where such a device governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a position) a travel region (st.travel_region, read only through the quantifier, as the abstract kind requires) the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). 'otherwise directed' admits any indication the officer gives there.

The section's own definition of 'preparing to move', read as s1 reads it: 'any indication that is visible to an approaching driver' is the vehicle visible from the subject (rel.visible) showing an indication; '(a) A movement of the vehicle' is its kin.speed above the halt tolerance; '(b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle' is sig.hand_signal ('a driver's or rider's arm signal') with a meaning other than no_signal; 'including, without limitation' admits further indications, of which a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator, 'the signal that precedes a manoeuvre') is the one the vocabulary carries. 'about to move' is an imminent movement read through these indications.

operationalizations.standard: Be prepared to stop
operationalizations.convention: stopping-distance model: the subject is prepared to stop where the distance it needs to come to 'complete cessation from movement' (the stop when required, DEF-NRS-484A-255) — its speed times the perception-reaction time plus its speed squared over twice the braking deceleration — does not exceed the gap between its body and the approached vehicle's (rel.surface_gap); the deceleration is selected by the surface: ice or snow, else a wet road or falling precipitation, else dry

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

residues.why: 'including, without limitation' lists examples of a vehicle moving or preparing to move; the duty is the same whether or not the vehicle is arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance). Some road user e, not the subject, that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle or an ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, shows a lit sig.warning_lamp of colour red, mode flashing, facing front; e is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) or preparing to move (rel.visible from the subject to e, and e's sig.hand_signal meaning other than no_signal or its sig.turn_indicator other than off); and e lies ahead of the subject (rel.bearing from the subject, longitudinal component positive) within p.emergency_approach_reach of centre distance (rel.centre_distance). Not applicable where a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a st.travel_region the subject occupies (rel.occupies).
obligation: Surrogate. For every road user e selected as in the applicability (re-bound with its whole selection: class, lamp, moving or preparing, ahead within the reach), the subject's stopping distance at the observation — kin.speed × p.driver_reaction_time plus kin.speed squared divided by twice the deceleration, the deceleration being p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_decel_dry — is at most the gap between the subject's body and e's (rel.surface_gap).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it

'preparing to move', which the section defines as an indication that the vehicle is 'about to move', is an imminent movement, read through the visible indications the definition lists (movement, hand signals) and a lit turn indicator
'visible to an approaching driver' is read as the vehicle being in the subject's line of sight (rel.visible), not as what the driver perceived
'prepared to stop' is read only as the ability to stop short of the approached vehicle at the current speed; readiness of mind is not observed and the rule is a surrogate

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry road. The subject vehicle moves toward an ambulance (authorized emergency vehicle) ahead of it within the approach reach; the ambulance moves with a red front warning lamp flashing. The subject's speed gives a stopping distance (reaction plus braking) longer than the surface gap to the ambulance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene, but the subject has slowed so that its stopping distance is shorter than the surface gap to the ambulance.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives at speed; no emergency or regulatory-agency vehicle is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone and does not arise.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe warning lamps, so whether the ambulance uses its flashing lights is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a police officer directing traffic (dev.human_direction, role police_officer) governs the lane the subject occupies.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Icy road (env.ice_or_snow). The subject's speed and gap would allow a stop on a dry surface but not at the ice deceleration; the ambulance ahead is stopped and its driver gives an arm signal, visible from the subject (preparing to move), with its red front lamp flashing.

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which a driver approaching an emergency or enforcement vehicle that shows flashing warning lamps counts as approaching it: about the distance at which the lamps are conspicuous by day and a driver at an urban speed of 15 m/s has ten seconds to slow
param_proposals.source: warning-lamp conspicuity and perception-reaction figures (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_267_2a)

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: source speed resolution (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B)

param_proposals.name: p.driver_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: perception-reaction time of an alert driver to an expected hazard in the stopping-distance model
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_600_1a)

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a dry paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.6)
param_proposals.source: tyre-road friction figures (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_wet
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a wet paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.4)
param_proposals.source: tyre-road friction figures (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.1)
param_proposals.source: tyre-road friction figures (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)

segmentation.text: Upon approaching an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
If the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle of a regulatory agency is moving in the same direction of travel as the driver,
not drive abreast of or overtake the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle of a regulatory agency.

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'an authorized emergency vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'), claimed as ru.aggregate; its 'not a stand-in for' a responding role does not bite, since the conduct the words require of it is read separately. 'an official vehicle of a regulatory agency' is ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, not read as an emergency vehicle. 'Upon approaching': the subject, moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance), has that vehicle ahead of it (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component positive) within the approach reach of centre distance (rel.centre_distance; no clearance is read from it). 'which is moving': the vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance; 'or preparing to move', as the section defines it (s9): the vehicle visible from the subject (rel.visible) showing an arm signal (sig.hand_signal meaning other than no_signal) or a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator left or right: the signal, not the manoeuvre). 'in any direction' adds no restriction. The vehicle is quantified in the formula, never a binder.

sig.warning_lamp: 'a warning lamp lit; colour ∈ {red, blue, amber, white}, mode ∈ {flashing, rotating, steady}, facing ∈ {front, rear, side}'. The words borrowed from DEF-NRS-484A-480-3, 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front', fix which lights meet the requirements: a lamp lit on the approached vehicle of colour red, mode flashing, facing front. Not a stand-in for an audible warning: no siren is read.

'any other vehicle' is the defined term vehicle, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); its exclusions are the reading's classification under that id. 'other' excludes the approached vehicle: the subject and it are not the same road user. 'the driver' is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

dev.human_direction: 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}': a law enforcement officer is role police_officer. The exception holds where such a device governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a position) a travel region (st.travel_region, through the quantifier) the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region').

'is moving' is the approached vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance; 'in the same direction of travel as the driver' is rel.same_direction ('headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance') between the subject and that vehicle, with the overtaking heading tolerance. 'the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle' is the vehicle s1 selects, re-bound with its whole selection.

'overtake' is drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, vehicle): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; it denotes the relative motion only, and the lanes are not read. 'drive abreast of' is the two side by side while the subject drives: the bodies' projections on the subject's heading share length (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero, 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)'; a projection, not a contact or a distance) with the subject's kin.speed above the halt tolerance. 'the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle' is the vehicle s1 selects, re-bound.

The section's own definition of 'preparing to move', read as s1 reads it: 'any indication that is visible to an approaching driver' is the vehicle visible from the subject (rel.visible) showing an indication; '(a) A movement of the vehicle' its kin.speed above the halt tolerance; '(b) The use of hand signals' sig.hand_signal meaning other than no_signal; 'including, without limitation' admits a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator). 'about to move' is an imminent movement read through these indications.

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

residues.why: 'including, without limitation' lists examples of a vehicle moving or preparing to move; the duty is the same whether or not the vehicle is arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. Some road user e, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle or an ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, was approached by the subject at some observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window (up to and including this one): there e showed a lit sig.warning_lamp red, flashing, facing front; e was moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) or preparing to move (rel.visible from the subject and e's sig.hand_signal other than no_signal or sig.turn_indicator other than off); e lay ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) within p.emergency_approach_reach (rel.centre_distance), the subject moving above p.halt_speed_tolerance; and at some observation of that window e was moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, tolerance p.overtake_same_direction_cos). For the overtaking alternative these trigger and condition observations lie between the act's onset and its recognition (occasion some_moment). Not applicable where a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a st.travel_region the subject occupies (rel.occupies) at every observation of the act (occasion throughout), or, for the abreast alternative, at the judged observation.
obligation: For every e selected as in the applicability (re-bound with its whole selection): (i) the subject does not drive abreast of e: it is not the case that the subject moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while the projections of the two bodies on the subject's heading share length (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero); and (ii) the subject does not overtake e: drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, e) with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos does not rise at the observation.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'preparing to move', defined as an indication that the vehicle is 'about to move', is an imminent movement read through the visible indications the definition lists and a lit turn indicator
'visible to an approaching driver' is read as the vehicle being in the subject's line of sight (rel.visible)
'drive abreast' is read as the two bodies side by side along the subject's heading while the subject moves; a subject at rest that the vehicle draws alongside does not drive abreast of it

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A fire engine (authorized emergency vehicle) moves ahead of the subject in the same direction with its red front lamp flashing; the subject approaches it from behind within the reach, draws alongside and passes it, the fire engine coming to be behind it.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene, but the subject stays behind the fire engine throughout, never sharing length with it along its heading.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes a slower car; no emergency or regulatory-agency vehicle is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone and does not arise.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe warning lamps.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the subject draws alongside the fire engine and keeps level with it, moving, without completing the pass.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The fire engine with its red lamp flashing moves in the opposite direction; the subject approaches it head-on and they come side by side as they meet. The headings are opposed, so the condition fails.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches the moving fire engine from behind within the reach at the onset of the pass; once alongside, the fire engine is no longer ahead, so the approach holds for part of the pass only; the pass is completed.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject approached the fire engine earlier, then halted; while the subject stands at rest the fire engine, lamps flashing, backs past it, so that relative to the subject it goes from ahead to behind. The subject was not moving at any observation of the act, so the approach held only before it began.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3
scenarios.narrative: The fire engine's red front lamp flashes at the onset of the subject's pass and is switched off midway; the pass is completed.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3_outside
scenarios.narrative: The fire engine's lamp flashed while the subject approached and was switched off before the pass began, outside the window behind its recognition; it stays off throughout the pass.

scenarios.name: occasion_s7
scenarios.narrative: The fire engine moves in the subject's direction at the onset of the pass and halts midway; the subject completes the pass.

scenarios.name: occasion_s7_outside
scenarios.narrative: The fire engine moved in the subject's direction long before, then halted on the roadway with its lamp flashing and visibly signalled with its driver's arm; it stays at rest throughout the subject's pass, which falls outside the window behind its last movement.

scenarios.name: occasion_s6
scenarios.narrative: A police officer directing traffic governs the subject's lane at the onset of the pass only; the subject completes the pass in a lane no officer governs.

scenarios.name: occasion_s6_outside
scenarios.narrative: A police officer directing traffic governs the lanes the subject occupies at every observation of the pass, and did not before it began; the officer waves the subject past.

under_way.words: overtake
under_way.justification: An observation inside the pass is one from the act's onset — the last observation of the window behind at which the vehicle was ahead of the subject with headings aligned, as drv.interaction.overtake_pass states it — to its recognition: there the subject moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) and the vehicle is no longer ahead clear of it, the bodies' projections on the subject's heading sharing length (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) or the vehicle being behind; before the onset the vehicle is ahead with no shared length.

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which a driver approaching an emergency or enforcement vehicle that shows flashing warning lamps counts as approaching it: about the distance at which the lamps are conspicuous by day and a driver at an urban speed of 15 m/s has ten seconds to slow
param_proposals.source: warning-lamp conspicuity and perception-reaction figures (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_267_2a)

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: source speed resolution (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B)

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: overtaking-duration figures (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_30_030)

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading figures (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_30_030)

segmentation.text: Upon approaching an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
If possible,
drive in a lane that is not adjacent to the lane in which the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle of a regulatory agency is moving,
unless roadway, traffic, weather or other conditions make doing so unsafe or impossible.

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'an authorized emergency vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); its 'not a stand-in for' a responding role does not bite, since the conduct is read separately. 'an official vehicle of a regulatory agency' is ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, not an emergency vehicle. 'Upon approaching': the subject, moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance), has that vehicle ahead of it (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) within the approach reach (rel.centre_distance; no clearance read). 'which is moving': the vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance; 'or preparing to move', as defined in s10: visible from the subject (rel.visible) with an arm signal (sig.hand_signal other than no_signal) or a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator: the signal, not the manoeuvre). 'in any direction' adds no restriction.

sig.warning_lamp: 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...'. The words borrowed from DEF-NRS-484A-480-3, 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front', fix the lights: a lamp lit of colour red, mode flashing, facing front. Not a stand-in for an audible warning: no siren is read.

'any other vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); exclusions are the reading's. 'other' excludes the approached vehicle. 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic ...; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}': a law enforcement officer is role police_officer; excepted where such a device governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

'drive in a lane' is the subject's footprint overlapping a lane (rel.occupies; st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles'), the lane being the subject's own feature; 'the lane in which the ... vehicle ... is moving' is a lane the approached vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane). 'adjacent' is read in two ways the contracts carry: the left or right neighbouring lane of the same direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction'; not the marking between the lanes), and, for a vehicle moving against the subject's direction, the two leftmost lanes of opposite directions — each of lane ordinal one (st.lane_adjacency ordinal, 'ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction'), their designated directions opposed (st.lane_direction) — on one and the same roadway that both road users occupy (st.roadway, 'separate roadways of a divided highway are separate', so a divided highway's opposing lanes are never adjacent). A lane is not adjacent to itself.

The section's definition of 'preparing to move', read as s1 reads it: visible from the subject (rel.visible); '(a) A movement of the vehicle' kin.speed above the halt tolerance; '(b) The use of hand signals' sig.hand_signal other than no_signal; 'including, without limitation' admits a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator). 'about to move' is read through these indications.

operationalizations.standard: If possible
operationalizations.convention: lane-change time: moving away from the vehicle's lane is possible once the approach has lasted the time a driver needs to perceive the vehicle and change one lane, and only where the subject's way carries a candidate lane: a lane on the same highway as the subject's lane (st.on_way) whose designated direction points the subject's way (st.lane_direction, positive dot product with the subject's lane direction) and that is not adjacent to the vehicle's lane

operationalizations.standard: unless roadway, traffic, weather or other conditions make doing so unsafe or impossible
operationalizations.convention: gap acceptance and lane availability: a candidate lane is impossible (roadway) where a temporary traffic control device governs it, and unsafe (traffic) where a road user occupying it, other than the subject (any road user using the highway: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances', DEF-NRS-484A-285, read without exclusion), is nearer the subject's body (rel.surface_gap) than the subject's speed times the following headway for the surface (ice or snow, else wet road or precipitation, else dry); weather makes the move unsafe where the road is icy or snow-covered, or the visibility (env.visibility) is shorter than the distance the subject travels at its speed in the lane-change time

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

residues.why: 'including, without limitation' lists examples of a vehicle moving or preparing to move; the duty is the same whether or not the vehicle is arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance). Some road user e, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle or an ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, shows a lit sig.warning_lamp red, flashing, facing front; e is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) or preparing to move (rel.visible from the subject and e's sig.hand_signal other than no_signal or sig.turn_indicator other than off); e lies ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) within p.emergency_approach_reach (rel.centre_distance). Not applicable where a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a st.travel_region the subject occupies (rel.occupies).
obligation: For every e selected as in the applicability for which that whole selection has held at every observation of the window behind of length p.emergency_lane_change_window, every st.lane Le that e occupies and every st.lane Ls that the subject occupies: Ls is not adjacent to Le, or the move is excused. Adjacent: Ls is the left or right neighbour of Le (st.lane_adjacency), or Ls and Le each have lane ordinal one (st.lane_adjacency ordinal) with designated directions (st.lane_direction) whose dot product is negative while some st.roadway is occupied (rel.occupies) by both the subject and e. Excused where env.ice_or_snow holds; or env.visibility is below the subject's kin.speed × p.emergency_lane_change_window; or no candidate lane is open and clear. A candidate lane C is a st.lane lying on (st.on_way) the same st.highway as Ls, whose designated direction has a positive dot product with Ls's, and which is not adjacent to Le in the sense above; C is open and clear where no dev.temporary_traffic_control governs it (dev.governs) and no road user u other than the subject occupying C has a rel.surface_gap to the subject below the subject's kin.speed × the headway (p.following_headway_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'preparing to move', defined as an indication that the vehicle is 'about to move', is read through the visible indications the definition lists and a lit turn indicator
'visible to an approaching driver' is read as the vehicle being in the subject's line of sight (rel.visible)

the catch-all 'other conditions' is read only through the contracts named: a closure by temporary traffic control, the gap to traffic occupying the candidate lane, ice or snow, a wet surface or precipitation, and visibility

adjacency across the centre of a two-way roadway is read only between the two leftmost lanes of opposite directions on one roadway; the vehicle's own lane is not adjacent to itself, so following it in its lane is not read as a breach of this paragraph

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry road, four lanes in the subject's direction. A police car (authorized emergency vehicle) with its red front lamp flashing moves in lane 1 ahead of the subject; the subject has been approaching it within the reach for longer than the lane-change window and stays in lane 2, the neighbour of lane 1, while lanes 3 and 4 are open and empty.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene, but the subject has moved to lane 3, which is not a neighbour of lane 1.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives in lane 2 of a four-lane carriageway; no emergency or regulatory-agency vehicle is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe lane adjacency, so whether the subject's lane neighbours the police car's lane, and which lanes are candidates, is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Two lanes in the subject's direction; the police car moves in lane 1 and the subject in lane 2. The only lane not adjacent to lane 1 is lane 1 itself, occupied by the police car within the headway gap, so no candidate lane is clear: excused.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the road is covered in snow (env.ice_or_snow): excused.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the approach has lasted less than the lane-change window when the subject is observed in lane 2.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: Undivided two-way roadway, two lanes each way. A regulatory-agency official vehicle with its red front lamp flashing moves against the subject in the leftmost lane of its direction; the subject, approaching it head-on, drives in the leftmost lane of its own direction, while the right lane of its direction is open and empty.

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which a driver approaching an emergency or enforcement vehicle that shows flashing warning lamps counts as approaching it: about the distance at which the lamps are conspicuous by day and a driver at an urban speed of 15 m/s has ten seconds to slow

segmentation.text: Upon approaching an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
If the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle of a regulatory agency:
(1) Approaches the driver’s vehicle,
proceed
as required pursuant to subsection 1 [NRS-484B-267-1a, NRS-484B-267-1b, NRS-484B-267-1c];
or (2) Stops,
proceed
as required pursuant to NRS 484B.607 [NRS-484B-607-1a, NRS-484B-607-1b, NRS-484B-607-1c, NRS-484B-607-1d].

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'an authorized emergency vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); its 'not a stand-in for' a responding role does not bite, the conduct being read separately. 'an official vehicle of a regulatory agency' is ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency. 'Upon approaching': the subject, moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance), has the vehicle ahead (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) within the approach reach (rel.centre_distance; no clearance read). 'which is moving': kin.speed above the halt tolerance; 'or preparing to move' (s12): visible from the subject (rel.visible) with an arm signal (sig.hand_signal) or a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator: the signal, not the manoeuvre). 'in any direction' adds no restriction.

sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...'; the words borrowed from DEF-NRS-484A-480-3, 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front', fix a lamp lit red, flashing, facing front. Not a stand-in for an audible warning: no siren is read.

'any other vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); 'other' excludes the approached vehicle; 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
dev.human_direction role police_officer ('a person directing traffic and the direction given'), governing (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

'Approaches the driver’s vehicle': the approached vehicle, moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance), has the subject's vehicle ahead of it (rel.bearing from that vehicle to the subject, 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component positive) within the approach reach of centre distance (rel.centre_distance; not a clearance). 'the driver’s vehicle' is the subject.

'proceed' is the subject's continued driving while the vehicle approaches it: its motion (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity'), which the rules of subsection 1 composed on s9r judge; the duty is the compliance those rules state, read at every observation at which the condition holds, the subject moving or not.

The section's definition of 'preparing to move', read as s1 reads it: visible from the subject (rel.visible); '(a) A movement of the vehicle' kin.speed above the halt tolerance; '(b) The use of hand signals' sig.hand_signal other than no_signal; 'including, without limitation' admits a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator).

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

residues.why: 'including, without limitation' lists examples of a vehicle moving or preparing to move; the duty is the same whether or not the vehicle is arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance). Some road user e, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle or an ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, shows a lit sig.warning_lamp red, flashing, facing front; e is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) or preparing to move (rel.visible from the subject and e's sig.hand_signal other than no_signal or sig.turn_indicator other than off); e lies ahead of the subject (rel.bearing from the subject, longitudinal component positive) within p.emergency_approach_reach (rel.centre_distance); and e approaches the subject's vehicle: e moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with the subject ahead of e (rel.bearing from e, longitudinal component positive) within p.emergency_approach_reach. Not applicable where a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a st.travel_region the subject occupies (rel.occupies).
obligation: The subject proceeds as subsection 1 requires: it complies with NRS_484B_267_1a, NRS_484B_267_1b_o1, NRS_484B_267_1b_o2 and NRS_484B_267_1c, each composed with its binder subject mapped to this node's subject (a composed rule not engaged counts as complied with).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'preparing to move', defined as an indication that the vehicle is 'about to move', is read through the visible indications the definition lists and a lit turn indicator
'visible to an approaching driver' is read as the vehicle being in the subject's line of sight (rel.visible)

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: An ambulance with its red front lamp flashing moves toward the subject head-on within the reach while the subject moves toward it; the subject keeps its lane and speed, neither yielding nor moving to the right-hand edge nor stopping, so a composed rule of subsection 1 is violated.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same approach; the subject moves to a position parallel to and close to the right-hand edge, clear of the intersection, and stops there until the ambulance has passed, complying with every composed rule.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives; no emergency or regulatory-agency vehicle is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe warning lamps.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject follows the ambulance, lamps flashing, which moves away ahead of it in the same direction: the subject approaches it but the ambulance does not approach the subject's vehicle.

segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall not intentionally interfere with the movement of
a person lawfully riding
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter.

elements.justification: 'a motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); the exclusions are the reading's classification under that id. 'The driver' is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'riding' is the ridden device moving: its kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') above the halt tolerance; the person on it is the device's rider and is not a separate road user in the scene. 'lawfully' is the lawfulness of the rider's own conduct under every rule engaged for it, which no atom carries and no composition of a named rule states: the gap on this span. The nearest atom, kin.speed, says only that the device moves, not that it moves lawfully.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride, having two tandem wheels ...'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts'), 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each is the admitted aggregate, claimed whole, never expanded into classes; the protected road user is a member of any of the three.

operationalizations.standard: intentionally interfere with the movement of
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the moving subject interferes with the rider's movement where its body touches the rider's (rel.contact), or where, the two centres closing within the conflict horizon to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance), the rider brakes harder than an evasive deceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal below its negative); intent is a state of mind, read only through this conduct

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. Some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, is being ridden: its kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, and it is ridden lawfully (the gap: no operator states that r complies with every rule engaged for it).
obligation: Surrogate. For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection), where the subject moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance): the subject is not in contact with r (rel.contact), and it is not the case that, the two approaching within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), r's longitudinal acceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal) is below the negative of p.rider_evasive_decel.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

'intentionally' is a state of mind no trace shows; the rule reads only the conduct that interferes: contact, or a closing conflict to which the rider answers with evasive braking. An evasive swerve without braking is not read

scenarios.name: permit

scenarios.name: idle

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe longitudinal acceleration, and the two bodies do not touch.

scenarios.name: branch_1

gaps.proposal: lawful (who : Arg) — a Formula that holds at an observation where the road user `who` complies there with every rule of the set engaged for it (its binders' classes and applicability holding with `who` as subject), unknown where one of them is unknown: it decides which riders the duty protects, the road users it concerns, from the lawfulness of their own conduct, which the words name without naming a rule
gaps.nearest: Formula.rule (another rule complied with) composes one named rule with a map of its binders: the words name no rule, and 'lawfully' refers to every rule engaged for the rider, so no finite composition written here states it; Formula.ruleApplies decides engagement only, not compliance.

segmentation.text: When overtaking or passing
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
proceeding in the same direction,
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall exercise due care and:
If there is more than one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction,
move the vehicle to the lane to the immediate left,
if the lane is available and moving into the lane is reasonably safe.

elements.justification: 'overtaking or passing' a road user proceeding the same way is drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; it denotes the relative motion only and says nothing of lanes, which the words here do not name. The pass is under way while the bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero: 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)'; a projection, not a contact or a distance), within the window behind the pass's recognition.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ...'), 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole; the overtaken road user is a member of any of them.

'proceeding' is the overtaken road user moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); 'in the same direction' is rel.same_direction ('headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance') between the subject and it, with the overtaking heading tolerance.

'a motor vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'). 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.standard: shall exercise due care
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the pass is made with due care where the subject's body never touches the overtaken rider's (rel.contact) and the rider is never made to brake harder than an evasive deceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal below its negative) while the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero); care is a state of mind, read only through this outcome

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. At the observation, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r) rises, with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos, for some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, which at some observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window was moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, tolerance p.overtake_same_direction_cos).
obligation: Surrogate. For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection): at every observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window, the subject is not in contact with r (rel.contact), and wherever the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) r's longitudinal acceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal) is not below the negative of p.rider_evasive_decel.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'due care' is read only through the pass's outcome for the rider: no contact and no evasive braking while side by side; other aspects of care are not observed and the rule is a surrogate

scenarios.name: idle

scenarios.name: blind

'more than one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction' is the count of lanes in the direction of a lane the overtaken road user occupies (st.lane_adjacency, 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction'; not the marking between lanes) being more than the stated one, read on a lane (st.lane) the rider occupies (rel.occupies). 'traffic' names the users of those lanes; no membership is read, the direction being the lanes' own.

'the vehicle' is the subject (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', of which the motor vehicle is a member). 'the lane to the immediate left' is the left neighbouring lane of the same direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction') of a lane (st.lane) the overtaken rider occupies (rel.occupies); 'move ... to' it is the subject's footprint overlapping that lane and not overlapping the rider's lane while the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), i.e. while it passes.

operationalizations.standard: if the lane is available and moving into the lane is reasonably safe
operationalizations.convention: gap acceptance at the start of the pass: at the last observation of the window behind at which the rider was ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, no shared length) with aligned headings, the lane to the rider's lane's immediate left exists (st.lane_adjacency), no temporary traffic control device governs it (available), and no road user other than the subject and the rider occupying it is nearer the subject's body (rel.surface_gap) than the subject's speed times the following headway for the surface: ice or snow, else wet road or precipitation, else dry (reasonably safe)

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. At the observation, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r) rises, with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos, for some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, which at some observation of that window was moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos); and at some observation of that window at which the two were side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), r occupied a st.lane whose count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) is more than the literal one.
obligation: For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection), unless the left lane was unavailable or unsafe at the pass's start: at every observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window at which the subject and r are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), the subject occupies (rel.occupies) the left neighbour (st.lane_adjacency) of a st.lane r occupies, and occupies no lane r occupies. The pass's start is the last observation of the window at which r was ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with headings aligned (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos); there the left lane is unavailable or unsafe where r's lane has no left neighbour, or a dev.temporary_traffic_control governs (dev.governs) that neighbour, or some road user u other than the subject and r occupying it has a rel.surface_gap to the subject below the subject's kin.speed × the headway (p.following_headway_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'move the vehicle to the lane' is read as the subject wholly in the left lane, overlapping none of the rider's lanes, at every observation at which it is side by side with the rider
'available' and 'reasonably safe' are read at the pass's start only, through closure by temporary traffic control and the time-headway gap to road users occupying the left lane

segmentation.text: When overtaking or passing
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
proceeding in the same direction,
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall exercise due care and:
If there is only one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction,
pass to the left of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter
at a safe distance, which must be not less than 3 feet between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter,
and shall not move again to the right side of the highway
until the vehicle is safely clear of the overtaken bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.
Except as otherwise provided in NRS 484B.213 and 484B.217 [NRS-484B-213-1, NRS-484B-213-2a, NRS-484B-213-2b, NRS-484B-213-2c, NRS-484B-217-2],

when passing to the left of a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter at a safe distance of not less than 3 feet between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter, this paragraph authorizes the driver, if it is safe, to pass: (1) To the left of the center of the highway. (2) In a no-passing zone.

elements.justification: 'overtaking or passing' a road user proceeding the same way is drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; it denotes the relative motion only. The pass is under way while the bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero; a projection, not a contact or a distance), within the window behind the pass's recognition.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole.
'proceeding' is the overtaken road user moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); 'in the same direction' is rel.same_direction ('headings aligned') between the subject and it.
'a motor vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'). 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.standard: shall exercise due care
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the pass is made with due care where the subject's body never touches the overtaken rider's (rel.contact) and the rider is never made to brake harder than an evasive deceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal below its negative) while the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero); care is a state of mind, read only through this outcome

residues.why: the authorization lets a driver passing a rider at the stated clearance pass left of the center or in a no-passing zone, conduct other rules (NRS 484B.213, 484B.217) forbid; it relaxes those rules and leaves the duties of this paragraph unchanged: the duty of care is the same whether or not the authorization holds

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. At the observation, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r) rises, with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos, for some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, which at some observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window was moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos). The authorization (b12), suspended where NRS_484B_213_1, NRS_484B_213_2a, NRS_484B_213_2b, NRS_484B_213_2c or NRS_484B_217_2 applies, does not change this duty.
obligation: Surrogate. For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection): at every observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window, the subject is not in contact with r (rel.contact), and wherever the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) r's longitudinal acceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal) is not below the negative of p.rider_evasive_decel.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'due care' is read only through the pass's outcome for the rider: no contact and no evasive braking while side by side; the rule is a surrogate

Here the pass is read while under way — the bodies side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero; a projection, not a contact or a distance) after the rider was ahead within the window — and once completed, from the observation at which the concept rises, within the window.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole.

'traffic' names the users of the lane; no membership is read.

The concept says nothing of whether the subject occupies L, so it reads a move back toward the rider's lane from the opposing lane or from the left part of the rider's lane alike. 'again' fixes the order: the subject first had the rider on its right.

operationalizations.standard: until the vehicle is safely clear of the overtaken bicycle
operationalizations.convention: time headway: the subject (the vehicle) is safely clear of the overtaken rider where the rider is behind it (rel.bearing longitudinal component negative, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with a gap between the bodies (rel.surface_gap) of at least the rider's speed times the following headway for the surface — ice or snow, else wet road or precipitation, else dry — so that the rider, following, keeps the headway a following road user keeps

residues.why: the authorization lets a driver passing a rider at the stated clearance pass left of the center or in a no-passing zone, conduct other rules (NRS 484B.213, 484B.217) forbid; it relaxes those rules and leaves the duty not to move back right before being clear unchanged

obligation: For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection), where r is not safely clear behind the subject — that is, not (r behind the subject, rel.bearing longitudinal component negative and rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, with rel.surface_gap at least r's kin.speed × the headway: p.following_headway_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry) — the subject does not move to the right: drv.lane.heading_right_of_carrier(subject, L) with sin_tol p.course_departure_sin_tol and speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance holds for no st.lane L that r occupies (rel.occupies).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

'move again to the right side of the highway' is read as the subject's heading turned to the right of the rider's lane direction beyond the course tolerance, after it has the rider on its right; a gradual drift within that tolerance is not read
'safely clear' is read as the rider behind the subject at a time-headway gap at the rider's speed; the rider's own braking ability is not otherwise read

segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any person riding
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
or a pedestrian
as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]
on the pathway or lane.
The driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive
within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;
(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;
(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;
(d) In the performance of official duties;
(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;
or
(f) In an emergency.

elements.justification: 'Motor vehicle' is admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-130: 'every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate' and is claimed with the admitted id, never expanded into classes, as the index maps 'The driver of a motor vehicle' for NRS_484B_270_1. 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080, 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is no aggregate: ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle', so the role is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency) and the atom reads the vehicle's class only.

Reuses the index mapping of 'shall yield' (kin.speed, rel.contact). To yield is to give the other precedence: what the subject does is its motion, kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity', read to tell a moving subject from one at rest; a failure that ends in a crash is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'. rel.contact is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss': the near miss is bounded by the operationalization of t3, not by this atom.

'Riding' is the rider's controlled motion of the device; the ontology reads who controls a road user's motion through that motion, so the person riding is the device moving: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance, as the index maps 'a person lawfully riding' for NRS_484B_270_1 (observable_reading, agency). kin.speed carries no exclusion that applies.

'Bicycle', 'electric bicycle' and 'electric scooter' are admitted aggregates (DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter); ru.aggregate is claimed with each admitted id, as the index maps 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter' for NRS_484B_270_2a_o1, and never replaced by ru.bicycle, ru.electric_bicycle or ru.electric_scooter.

'Pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); claimed as ru.aggregate with that id, as the index maps 'A pedestrian' for NRS_484B_297_6_o1.

'the pathway or lane' is the pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters the line names: st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'. The other road user is on it: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', which anchors the lane to that road user so the rule reads its own lane l and not any lane of the scene; the obligation reads the same l again for the subject. Neither contract states an exclusion that applies.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where the two approach 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle (ru.aggregate), read as driven through its controlled motion.
obligation: For every road user p of the scene other than the subject, and every bicycle lane or path l (st.bicycle_lane_or_path) whose region p's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) at the observation, where p is either (i) a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter moving with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance, or (ii) a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian to whom NRS_484B_297_6_o1 applies (ruleApplies, its subject mapped to p): the subject's body is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject's footprint overlaps that same l while the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance and prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Read at every observation; an unobserved occupancy, contact or closest approach leaves the verdict unknown where it decides it.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observed, and the duty binds the vehicle's conduct.
'a person riding' is read as the device moving above the halt tolerance: a rider halted in the lane is not read as riding.

The yield is read on the lane the other occupies: the subject fails to yield where it touches the other, or where its footprint overlaps that lane while it moves with a conflicting closest approach to the other; a conflict while the subject stays outside that lane is not read as a failure to yield on the pathway or lane.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car (member of the motor vehicle aggregate) turning right moves across a bicycle lane; its footprint overlaps the lane while a moving bicycle in that lane closes from behind, their closest approach falling within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car halts short of the bicycle lane until the moving bicycle has gone by, then crosses the lane; while it overlaps the lane there is no contact and no conflicting closest approach with any rider in it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a bicycle (not a member of the motor vehicle aggregate) riding in the bicycle lane behind another bicycle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car's footprint is near the bicycle lane while a moving electric scooter closes on it with a conflicting closest approach; the source does not observe footprint occupancy, so whether the scooter is on the lane and whether the car overlaps it are unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses the bicycle lane into a driveway; no bicycle, electric bicycle, electric scooter or pedestrian is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks in the bicycle lane while the sidewalk beside it is clear and unobstructed, so NRS_484B_297_6_o1 does not apply to it; the car enters the lane with a conflicting closest approach to the pedestrian but no contact.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As branch_2, except that the pedestrian has stepped from the sidewalk into the bicycle lane to move around an obstruction on the sidewalk, so NRS_484B_297_6_o1 applies to it.

segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any person riding
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
or a pedestrian
as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]
on the pathway or lane.
The driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive
within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;
(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;
(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;
(d) In the performance of official duties;
(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;
or
(f) In an emergency.

elements.justification: 'Motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); ru.aggregate is claimed with the admitted id. 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role, not membership (ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'): it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

Every verb is a way of having the vehicle's footprint in the lane: to enter is its footprint coming to overlap the lane, to drive within it is to overlap it while moving, and to stop, stand or park is to overlap it while halted. 'Stop' here is prohibited, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 states its own scope ('when prohibited, any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'); 'stand' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle') and 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle') are halts too. Moving and halted together are every observation of the footprint in the lane, so the prohibition is read on rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', of a st.bicycle_lane_or_path region, whatever the motion; no exclusion of either contract applies. The exceptions of DEF-NRS-484A-260 ('to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer') coincide with exceptions (c) and (e) and are carried there.

'a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; 'within' it is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', which anchors the lane l to the subject. 'Provided' is the status of a feature, read through the lane's presence (observable_reading, status).

'Alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015, 'a highway: (1) Within a city block set apart for public use ... (2) Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; 'driveway' (DEF-NRS-484A-190, 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel') meets the highway at st.driveway_or_alley_entrance, 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'. That atom is 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there', a distinction the exception does not need, since it covers alley and driveway alike. Entering or exiting is read through the subject's footprint (rel.occupies): its stretch in the lane l runs until its footprint overlaps such a region (entering), or has run since an observation at which it overlapped one (exiting).

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): sig.hazard is 'both indicators flashing together', a signal, not the vehicle's condition; kin.engine_running is 'propulsion is available', 'Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt'. Neither denotes a disabled vehicle, and the condition of a road user is never an assumption.

'Traffic' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'). The purpose 'to avoid conflict' is read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading, purpose): at the observation at which the subject's footprint came to overlap the lane (rel.occupies rising), a member of traffic other than the subject was in conflict with it, prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. The primitives are 'Not a stand-in for: contact between bodies, the clearance between bodies, or the danger of a crash ... alone': they bound a traffic conflict under the conflict convention, which is what the words name, not a contact.

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): ru.emergency_vehicle ('vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency', 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle') and ru.official_vehicle ('a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment') state what the vehicle is, never what it is doing; sig.warning_lamp ('a warning lamp lit') is shown by vehicles on duty and off it alike, and many official duties (a patrol, an inspection, a delivery of mail) show none. No conduct or feature the ontology carries tells a vehicle performing official duties from one that is not.

'Police officer' (DEF-NRS-484A-180, 'every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic') directing traffic is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}', with role police_officer; the direction reaches the subject where it governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region, the abstract union of the kinds dev.governs admits, among them the bicycle lane or path) whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), as the index maps 'or the directions of a police officer'. dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position': it is read as control of the region, not as where the subject must halt. The officer's authority is read through the direction's presence (observable_reading, status).

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): sig.hazard is a signal, not a peril; ru.emergency_vehicle is a class and 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle'. Neither denotes an emergency, which is never an assumption.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven, and its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a bicycle lane or path l (st.bicycle_lane_or_path) at the observation.
obligation: At that observation one of the exceptions holds for the same l: (a) the subject's footprint overlaps l at every observation until one at which it overlaps an alley (st.alley) or a driveway or alley entrance (st.driveway_or_alley_entrance) (until), or has overlapped l at every observation since one at which it overlapped such a region (since); (b) [gap: a disabled vehicle]; (c) at the observation at which the subject's footprint came to overlap l (the latest rise of its overlap, read with since), some road user u other than the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, had prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; (d) [gap: the vehicle in the performance of official duties]; (e) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a travel region whose region the subject's footprint overlaps; (f) [gap: an emergency]. Where none holds, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.
'provided' for bicycles is the lane's legal status, read through the presence of the mapped bicycle lane or path.
The purpose 'to avoid conflict' is read through the conduct it explains: a conflict with other traffic at the moment the subject came into the lane.
The officer's authority is read through the presence of a person directing traffic in the police_officer role.
Entering, stopping, standing, parking and driving within the lane are read together as any overlap of the subject's footprint with the lane, since together they cover every motion state.

gaps.nearest: ru.emergency_vehicle and ru.official_vehicle (classes: what a vehicle is, not what it is doing); sig.warning_lamp (a lamp lit, shown on and off duty alike). The exception decides whether a motor vehicle may enter, stand in or move through a bicycle lane, which only the duty being performed decides.

gaps.proposal: ru.disabled | a vehicle that cannot move under its own power or cannot be driven on (a breakdown, crash damage, a flat tyre), as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** a halt, a set parking brake or lit hazard lamps — a vehicle at rest with its hazards lit may be fully operable | general
gaps.nearest: sig.hazard (both indicators flashing together: a signal a driver chooses to emit, not the vehicle's condition); kin.engine_running (propulsion available; 'Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt', and a disabled vehicle may still run its engine). The exception decides whether a motor vehicle may stand in or move through a bicycle lane, which the vehicle's condition, not its signals, decides.

gaps.proposal: env.emergency | a sudden peril at the observation that a road user's conduct answers to (a fire, a medical emergency, a crash or a hazard ahead), as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** an emergency vehicle's class, its lamps or its siren | general
