segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsection 3 [NRS-484B-270-3],
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter or proceed through an intersection
while driving within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters.

elements.justification: Reuses the index mapping of 'the driver of a motor vehicle' (NRS_484B_270_2a_o1): the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), since ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.

'Intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105, 'The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of the roadways of two highways which join one another'; '(3) The junction of an alley with a street, road or highway shall not constitute an intersection') is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges; a junction where an alley meets another way ... is no intersection', whose exclusion of the alley junction is the definition's own. It is 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk or a stop line': the words name the intersection itself. Entering it and proceeding through it are the subject's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies) while moving.

'a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; 'within' it is rel.occupies, which anchors that lane to the subject. 'Driving' is the vehicle's controlled motion, read as kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance (observable_reading, agency). No exclusion of these contracts applies.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a bicycle lane or path (st.bicycle_lane_or_path) at the observation.
obligation: At that observation the subject's footprint overlaps no intersection (st.intersection), or NRS_484B_270_3_o2 is complied with by the subject at that observation (rule, subject mapped to subject): what subsection 3 otherwise provides is its exceptions, under which the subject may drive within the lane, through the intersection included. Where the subject overlaps an intersection and that rule is violated, the duty is violated; where either is unknown and the other does not decide, unknown.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.
'driving within' is read as the vehicle moving above the halt tolerance with its footprint overlapping the lane.
Entering and proceeding through an intersection are read at every observation at which the moving subject's footprint overlaps both the bicycle lane or path and an intersection.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car drives along a bicycle lane and enters an intersection from it; no exception of subsection 3 holds (no alley or driveway, no conflict at its entry into the lane, not an emergency or official vehicle, no officer directing).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A police officer directing traffic governs the bicycle lane; at the officer's direction a car drives within the lane and proceeds through the intersection, complying with NRS_484B_270_3_o2 under its exception (e).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car in the general travel lane enters the intersection; its footprint never overlaps the bicycle lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car drives along the edge of a bicycle lane into an intersection with no exception present; footprint occupancy is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car drives within the bicycle lane and turns into a driveway before reaching the intersection; its footprint never overlaps an intersection.

segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall: Exercise due care
to avoid a collision
with a person riding
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter.

elements.justification: Reuses the index mapping of 'The driver of a motor vehicle' (NRS_484B_270_1): the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.
A collision is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; it is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss', which the operationalization of w2 bounds separately.

'a person riding' is the rider's controlled motion of the device, read as the device moving: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance (observable_reading, agency), as the index maps 'a person lawfully riding' for NRS_484B_270_1.

Reuses the index mapping of 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter.' (NRS_484B_270_1): the three admitted aggregates, claimed as ru.aggregate with their ids, never expanded into class atoms.

operationalizations.standard: due care to avoid a collision (a standard of the driver's care, a state of mind)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves, care shows in its keeping no closest approach to the rider, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every road user b other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter and moving with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance: the subject is not in contact with b (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, b) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, b) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of care, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.
'a person riding' is read as the device moving above the halt tolerance; a rider at rest is not read.

Due care, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome while the subject moves: no contact and no conflicting closest approach with a riding bicyclist or scooter rider; lookout, speed choice and every other aspect of care are read only through that outcome.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
shall not: Intentionally
interfere with the movement
of a motor vehicle.

elements.justification: The three admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, claimed as ru.aggregate with their ids as the index maps 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'; 'the operator' is read through the device's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role'.

'Motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'), claimed as ru.aggregate, as the index maps 'any motor vehicle'.

The movement of the motor vehicle is its motion: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the vehicle moving, above p.halt_speed_tolerance) and kin.accel_longitudinal 'acceleration along heading, signed', whose braking shows the movement disturbed; it is 'Not a stand-in for: speed', and it is read here as the change the interference forces, not as the speed. The rider interferes from in front of the vehicle's movement: rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame', with the rider's bearing in the vehicle's frame pointing ahead. No exclusion applies.

operationalizations.standard: intentionally interfere (intent, a state of mind, and the degree of interference)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: an interference with a vehicle's movement is a conflict in which the vehicle, with the rider ahead of it, brakes evasively — a deceleration beyond comfortable service braking while their closest approach lies within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, read as operated.
obligation: At every observation, for every road user m other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle and moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), it is not the case that: the subject lies ahead of m (the longitudinal component of the subject's rel.bearing in m's frame is positive), m's kin.accel_longitudinal is at or below the negative of p.vehicle_evasive_decel, and prim.closest_approach_within(m, subject) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(m, subject) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion; who controls it is not observed.

Intent shows in no single observation: it is read only through the conduct that interferes — the rider ahead of a moving motor vehicle in a conflict that forces it to brake evasively — and a conflict the rider did not seek is not told apart; an interference that forces no evasive braking (a swerve only) is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle cuts in front of a moving car and slows; the car, with the bicycle ahead of it, brakes harder than p.vehicle_evasive_decel while their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides in a bicycle lane; a car passes it without braking and without a conflicting closest approach.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a car (not a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregates).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter swerves in front of a moving car with a conflicting closest approach; the car's longitudinal acceleration is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a path with no motor vehicle in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.vehicle_evasive_decel
param_proposals.convention: the longitudinal deceleration of a motor vehicle at or beyond which its braking counts as an evasive reaction to another road user rather than ordinary speed control: about 0.4 g, above the comfortable deceleration of about 3.4 m/s^2
param_proposals.source: AASHTO comfortable deceleration rate; traffic-conflict studies of evasive braking

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (time-to-collision thresholds)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO)

segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
shall not: Overtake and pass a motor vehicle
unless the operator can do so safely without endangering himself or herself or the occupants of the motor vehicle.

elements.justification: The three admitted aggregates, claimed as ru.aggregate with their ids, as the index maps 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'; 'the operator' is read through the device's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role'.

'Overtake and pass' is drv.interaction.overtake_pass, whose contract is 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it', with a the subject and b the motor vehicle, as the index maps 'approaching from the rear shall not overtake and pass such stopped vehicle'; it 'says nothing of the lanes they occupy, of whether b moves', so a pass of a moving or a standing motor vehicle is covered alike. 'A motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, claimed as ru.aggregate.

operationalizations.standard: safely, without endangering the operator or the occupants of the motor vehicle
operationalizations.convention: bicyclist operating space: a pass is safe where the gap between the rider's body and the passed vehicle's body stays at least the rider's operating-space sway and the bodies never touch; traffic-conflict technique: no other road user comes into a closest approach within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance during the pass

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, read as operated.
obligation: For every road user m other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle: at each observation at which drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, m) with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos holds (the pass's recognition), the pass was safe at every observation since its beginning — the last observation of the window behind at which m was ahead of the subject (positive longitudinal component of m's rel.bearing in the subject's frame, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with headings aligned within p.overtake_same_direction_cos (rel.same_direction), read with since: at each such observation the subject is not in contact with m (rel.contact), its rel.surface_gap to m is at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap, and no road user u other than the subject and m has prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Where the pass is recognized and the pass was not safe throughout, violated; an unobserved gap, contact or closest approach that decides it leaves it unknown.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion; who controls it is not observed.
'can do so safely' is the operator's judgement of the pass, read through the pass actually made: its clearance and the conflicts during it.

Endangering the occupants of the motor vehicle is read through the clearance to and contact with its body, which carries them; endangering the operator is read through that clearance and through conflicting closest approaches with every other road user during the pass; other hazards (the surface, the operator's speed) are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle overtakes and passes a car moving slowly in the same direction, keeping a gap between bodies smaller than p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap while alongside.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle overtakes and passes a slow car with a gap of at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap throughout the pass, no contact and no conflicting closest approach with any other road user.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a car (not a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregates) overtaking another car.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle overtakes and passes a car with no conflict with other road users; the gap between bodies is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle begins the pass of a car with a wide gap, then closes to a gap below p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap while still alongside before clearing the car: the pass is safe for part of the act only.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle follows close behind a car with a small gap before the pass begins, then moves out and keeps a gap of at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap at every observation from the pass's beginning to its recognition.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a street with no motor vehicle in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle overtakes and passes a standing car with a wide gap, but during the pass an oncoming car comes into a closest approach with the bicycle within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (bicyclist operating space)

segmentation.text: A driver of a motor vehicle
shall: Exercise due care
to avoid a collision
with a pedestrian.

elements.justification: The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.
A collision is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; it is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss', which the operationalization of x2 bounds separately.

'Pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate as the index maps 'A pedestrian'.

operationalizations.standard: due care to avoid a collision (a standard of the driver's care, a state of mind)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves, care shows in its keeping no closest approach to the pedestrian, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every road user p other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of care, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'A driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.

Due care, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome while the subject moves: no contact and no conflicting closest approach with a pedestrian; lookout, speed choice and every other aspect of care are read only through that outcome.

segmentation.text: A driver of a motor vehicle
shall: Exercise
proper caution
upon observing
a pedestrian:
(1) On or near a highway, street or road;
(2) At or near a bus stop or bench, shelter or transit stop for passengers of public mass transportation
or in the act of boarding
a bus or other public transportation vehicle;
or (3) In or near a school zone or a school crossing zone
marked in accordance with NRS 484B.363
or a marked or unmarked crosswalk.

elements.justification: The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.

What the driver must exercise shows in the vehicle's conduct toward the observed pedestrian: its motion, kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the duty read while it moves above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and the outcome caution exists to prevent, rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', which is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss'; the near miss is bounded by the operationalization of z2.

Observing is a perception; the ontology reads what was in an actual road user's line of sight as rel.visible, 'b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight from a's reference point to b's body' (observable_reading, perception). Its exclusions — a distance, the sight distance of a place, the clarity of the air, a lamp being lit — do not apply: the words name what the driver could see of an actual pedestrian.

'Pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate.

'Highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic'), 'street' (DEF-NRS-484A-265, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city') and 'road' (DEF-NRS-484A-215, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway outside the territorial limits of a city') are all highways, and together every highway whatever the city limits: st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; it is 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway', and the words name the whole way. 'On' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; 'near' is st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)', at most p.pedestrian_near_reach. st.region_geometry is 'Not a stand-in for: occupancy', which is why rel.occupies carries 'on'.

'a bus stop or bench, shelter or transit stop for passengers of public mass transportation' is st.transit_stop, 'a bus stop, bench, shelter or platform for public transport passengers'. 'Stop' here is part of the place name 'bus stop' and 'transit stop', not the halt DEF-NRS-484A-255 or DEF-NRS-484A-260 defines. 'At' is rel.occupies of the stop's region and 'near' is its st.region_geometry ground distance at most p.pedestrian_near_reach, which also anchors the stop to the pedestrian.

Boarding is read through the conduct that shows it (observable_reading, purpose): the pedestrian within p.pedestrian_near_reach of the vehicle's body, rel.surface_gap 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', while the vehicle is at rest, drv.motion.complete_halt 'The road user is at rest at the observation', and has a door open, sig.door_open 'a door open'. The halt concept 'says nothing of how long the road user stays at rest, where it is, or why', which the reading does not need.

'Bus' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus ('a vehicle owned by the State, a political subdivision or a private school or nursery, designed for carrying more than 10 passengers ... or a vehicle, other than a taxicab, designed and used for the transportation of persons for compensation'), claimed as ru.aggregate. 'Other public transportation vehicle' is a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported ... upon a highway', excluding devices 'used exclusively upon stationary rails') that is in public transit service: ru.transit_bus, 'bus in public transit service, identifiable by its livery or route display', a class the words name on their own and no definition admits.

'School zone' (DEF-NRS-484B-063, 'those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property') and 'school crossing zone' (DEF-NRS-484B-060, 'those sections of streets not adjacent to school property that pupils cross while following a designated walking route to school') are administrative categories; the law takes them where they are 'marked', and the ontology makes the sign the atom where a category is marked on the road: dev.zone_sign, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}', with kind school or school_crossing and its end attribute false; the sections of street are the travel regions it governs, dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', of kind st.travel_region. dev.zone_sign is 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now', which the words do not ask: the zone, not its hours, places the pedestrian. 'In' is rel.occupies of such a region and 'near' its st.region_geometry ground distance at most p.pedestrian_near_reach.

'marked in accordance with NRS 484B.363' is the zone's marking: dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing. Its accordance with NRS 484B.363, a statute outside this corpus, is the legal status of a feature, read through the sign's presence (observable_reading, status).

'Crosswalk' (DEF-NRS-484A-065, '(1) That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface') is st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute', both values of the attribute read since the words name 'a marked or unmarked crosswalk'. 'In or near' (carried from z9) is rel.occupies of the crosswalk or its st.region_geometry ground distance at most p.pedestrian_near_reach.

operationalizations.standard: proper caution upon observing a pedestrian (a standard of the driver's care, a state of mind)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves, caution shows in its keeping no contact and no closest approach to the observed pedestrian, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every road user p other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, visible from the subject at that observation (rel.visible), and at one of the places: (1) p's footprint overlaps a highway (st.highway) or its ground distance to one (st.region_geometry) is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach; (2) p's footprint overlaps a transit stop (st.transit_stop) or its ground distance to one is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach, or p's rel.surface_gap to a road user v that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus, or a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that is an ru.transit_bus, is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach while v is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) and has a door open (sig.door_open); (3) p's footprint overlaps, or its ground distance is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach to, a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing that begins a zone, or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk, marked or unmarked): the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of caution, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'A driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.
'upon observing' is read as the pedestrian being in the subject's line of sight at the observation judged; a pedestrian seen earlier and occluded now is not read.
'in the act of boarding' is read through the conduct that shows it: the pedestrian close to a halted bus or transit vehicle with a door open.
the marking's accordance with NRS 484B.363 is read through the presence of the school or school-crossing zone sign.

Proper caution, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome while the subject moves: no contact and no conflicting closest approach with the observed pedestrian; slowing, lookout and every other aspect of caution are read only through that outcome.

segmentation.text: Except as provided in NRS 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B]:
Between adjacent intersections
at which official traffic-control devices are in operation
pedestrians
shall not cross at any place
except in a marked crosswalk.

elements.justification: 'Intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105, 'The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of the roadways of two highways which join one another') is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet', alley junctions excluded as the definition's (3) excludes them. 'Adjacent intersections' are two intersections with none between them along the way; the pedestrian is between them where its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) recorded as a directed approach to one of them, i1: st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', the carrier being 'the stretch one direction of travel uses to reach one junction' — so nothing lies between c's stretch and i1 — and the other, i2 ≠ i1, is reached either through a second carrier the pedestrian also occupies that enters i2 (the opposing direction of a two-way way), or, where c is a lane (st.lane), through a lane that enters i2 and leads into c, directly or through one lane between (st.lane_connectivity, 'which lane a lane leads into'). The relation atoms tie both intersections to the pedestrian's own carriers; no distance stands for belonging. A pedestrian at either intersection is not between them: its footprint overlaps neither i1 nor i2, nor a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier it occupies (st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'). st.lane_enters is 'Not a stand-in for: ... the region a device governs', which v3 reads separately.

'Official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'). The law's own words 'are in operation' qualify the devices and limit which members the duty reads: a device in operation is one that operates, displaying indications, so they leave out signs and markings, which are posted or painted but do not operate, and signal heads that are not operating — covered, dark, or inoperative. The members read are signal heads: dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {...}; uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered') with its uncovered attribute true and a state other than dark, and not dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'). The device is at the intersection where it governs it, dev.governs 'an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', or governs a carrier recorded as entering it (st.lane_enters), as the st.lane_enters contract directs: 'which intersection a device controls is read through both, or directly where the device governs the intersection'; dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position'. 'Official' is the device's legal status, read through its presence (observable_reading, status). Each of i1 and i2 must have such a device.

'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate as the index maps 'No pedestrian'.

To cross is to move across the way: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, 'Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r', with r the carrier c the pedestrian's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), as the index maps 'crossing a roadway' for LVMC_11_30_060_A. The concept 'says nothing of whether a occupies r', which rel.occupies supplies; a pedestrian at rest or walking along the carrier is not crossing, as the concept excludes.

'a marked crosswalk' is st.crosswalk with its marked attribute true ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute'), DEF-NRS-484A-065 (2) 'Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface'; 'in' it is rel.occupies of that crosswalk by the pedestrian, as the index maps 'except in a crosswalk'.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; neither LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 nor LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 applies to it (ruleApplies, subject mapped to subject); and at the observation it is between adjacent controlled intersections: its footprint overlaps a travel region c (rel.occupies) recorded as entering an intersection i1 (st.lane_enters), and an intersection i2 other than i1 is found either because its footprint also overlaps a travel region recorded as entering i2, or because c is a lane and a lane that enters i2 leads into c (st.lane_connectivity) directly or through one lane between; each of i1 and i2 has a device in operation — a dev.traffic_signal that is uncovered, whose state is not dark and that is not dev.inoperative — that governs it (dev.governs) or governs a travel region recorded as entering it; and its footprint overlaps neither i1 nor i2 nor a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier it occupies (st.entrance_of); and it is moving across c (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, c) with p.halt_speed_tolerance and p.crossing_motion_cos).
obligation: At that observation the subject's footprint overlaps a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) whose marked attribute is true (rel.occupies). Otherwise violated; where the crosswalk's occupancy or its marking is unobserved, unknown.

narrowings.why: 'official' is the devices' legal status, read through the presence of the signal heads.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Mid-block between two intersections each governed by an operating traffic signal, a pedestrian walks across both directional carriers of the roadway, outside any crosswalk.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Between the same two signalized intersections, a pedestrian walks across the roadway within a marked mid-block crosswalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks across a roadway mid-block between two intersections controlled only by stop signs, with no signal head at either.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses mid-block outside any crosswalk between two intersections with signal heads; which regions the signal heads govern is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses at the unmarked crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of the approach into a signalized intersection: it is at the intersection, not between.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian who is not blind approaches a person carrying a white cane while crossing mid-block between two signalized intersections, so LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 applies to it.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: pedestrian crossing-path geometry

segmentation.text: Except as provided in NRS 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B]:
A pedestrian
shall not cross an intersection diagonally
unless authorized by official traffic-control devices.

elements.justification: 'Pedestrian' is defined by DEF-NRS-484A-165 ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); the run admits it as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, claimed whole and never expanded into class atoms.

'intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105: 'The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines') is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'; the alley-junction exclusion of the definition's (3) is made by the atom's own contract. rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors the pedestrian in that intersection. 'diagonally' is a direction of the pedestrian's motion relative to the ways that meet there: the lanes that run into the intersection are read through st.lane_enters ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; kind st.lane), and drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, whose contract compares the road user's velocity with a carrier's designated direction, is read at two tolerances on every such lane: across it with the tolerance that tells across from along, and not across it with the right-angle tolerance, so the motion is oblique to both crossing ways. st.lane_enters is not used for the subject's presence (that is rel.occupies) nor for governance.

An 'official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-145) includes every 'marking ... placed or erected by a public authority ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'; the marking that authorizes a pedestrian crossing is a crosswalk 'distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface' (DEF-NRS-484A-065 (2)), carried by st.crosswalk ('marked crossing ...; marked attribute') read with its marked attribute; rel.occupies anchors the pedestrian inside that marked crossing. st.crosswalk 'Not a stand-in for' clauses do not concern this use.

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps an intersection x (rel.occupies, st.intersection) into which at least one lane runs (st.lane_enters); the duty does not apply where LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject.
obligation: At each such observation: if the subject moves diagonally across x, that is, for every lane l with st.lane_enters(l, x), drv_motion_moving_across_carrier(subject, l) holds with parameters (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.crossing_motion_cos) and does not hold with parameters (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.right_angle_crossing_cos), then the subject's footprint overlaps a marked crosswalk (st.crosswalk with its marked attribute true). Otherwise compliant.

narrowings.why: 'cross ... diagonally' is read at each observation as the pedestrian, inside the intersection, moving oblique to every lane that runs into it (neither within the right-angle tolerance of across a lane nor along it); a crossing is judged by its motion at each observation, not as a corner-to-corner path.
'official' is read through the presence of the marking on the road: a marked crosswalk in the scene is presumed placed by a public authority.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Lanes running into intersection x run north-south and east-west; a pedestrian inside x walks north-east at 1.4 m/s, oblique to every entering lane, with no crosswalk under its footprint.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian inside x near its edge walks east at 1.4 m/s: across the north-south lanes at right angles, so the motion is not diagonal.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian walks along a sidewalk and its footprint overlaps no intersection.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian is inside x with no marked crosswalk under it, but its velocity is not observed, so whether it moves diagonally cannot be told.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian inside x walks north-east within a marked diagonal crosswalk.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability in naturalistic crossing studies

param_proposals.name: p.right_angle_crossing_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as at right angles to the curb: within about 15 degrees of perpendicular
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability in naturalistic crossing studies

segmentation.text: Except as provided in NRS 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B]:
When authorized to cross diagonally,
pedestrians
shall cross only in accordance with the official traffic-control devices pertaining to such crossing movements.

elements.justification: 'cross diagonally' is read as in NRS_484B_287_1d: the pedestrian's footprint overlaps an intersection (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') and its velocity is oblique to every lane that runs into it (st.lane_enters, kind st.lane), read through drv.motion.moving_across_carrier at the along/across tolerance and the right-angle tolerance. 'authorized' by official traffic-control devices (DEF-NRS-484A-145: every 'sign, signal, marking and device') is read through the marking that indicates the crossing: a marked crosswalk (st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing'; DEF-NRS-484A-065 (2) 'distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings') under the pedestrian's footprint. The crossing begins where the footprint comes to overlap the intersection.
'pedestrians' (DEF-NRS-484A-165: 'a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...') is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

The devices 'pertaining to such crossing movements' that regulate a pedestrian's crossing are pedestrian signal heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute when a timer is displayed'). The head pertaining to the pedestrian's diagonal movement is the one the pedestrian faces across the crossing: its position (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') lies ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is used as the head's location, not as a stop line or crossing, which its 'Not a stand-in for' clause excludes. 'in accordance with' is read through the indication shown when the crossing begins: walk, or a flashing indication with a countdown, accords; a steady don't-walk or a flashing one without countdown does not.

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) beginning an authorized diagonal crossing: at this observation its footprint comes to overlap an intersection x (rel.occupies, st.intersection) that it did not overlap at the previous observation, its footprint overlaps a marked crosswalk (st.crosswalk, marked), and it moves diagonally across x: for every lane l with st.lane_enters(l, x) (at least one exists), drv_motion_moving_across_carrier(subject, l) holds with (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.crossing_motion_cos) and does not hold with (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.right_angle_crossing_cos). The duty does not apply where LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject.
obligation: For every pedestrian signal head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) that the subject faces at this observation, d shows neither dont_walk_steady nor dont_walk_flashing without its countdown attribute. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from the subject's kin.position to d's dev.position and h the subject's kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where no head is faced, compliant.

narrowings.why: 'official' is read through the presence of the signal head in the scene.

'cross only in accordance with the devices' is read at the start of the diagonal crossing (the entry into the intersection) through the indication of the pedestrian signal heads the pedestrian faces: a steady don't-walk, or a flashing don't-walk with no countdown, forbids starting; conduct later in the crossing is not read, and devices other than pedestrian signal heads are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: At an intersection with a marked diagonal crosswalk, a pedestrian steps from the corner into the intersection walking north-east inside the marking while the pedestrian head ahead of it, 25 m away within the facing cone, shows dont_walk_steady.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same entry, while the faced head shows walk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian enters the intersection walking east, at right angles to the north-south lanes: no diagonal crossing begins.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same entry as forbid, but the state of the faced pedestrian head is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Same entry while the faced head shows dont_walk_flashing with its countdown displayed.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Same entry while the faced head shows dont_walk_flashing without a countdown.

param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability in naturalistic crossing studies

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_cos

param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08; AASHTO Green Book urban cross-section widths

segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are not in place or not in operation,
the driver of a vehicle
shall yield the right-of-way,
slowing down or stopping if need be so to yield,
to a pedestrian crossing the highway within a crosswalk
when the pedestrian is upon the half of the highway upon which the vehicle is traveling or onto which the vehicle is turning,
or when the pedestrian is approaching so closely from the opposite half of the highway as to be in danger.

As used in this section, “half of the highway” means all traffic lanes of a highway which are designated for traffic traveling in one direction, and includes the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway.

elements.justification: The official traffic-control devices (DEF-NRS-484A-145: every 'sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic') that regulate a crosswalk crossing are the vehicular signal heads (dev.traffic_signal, state including 'dark') and pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal, state including 'dark') that control the travel regions the vehicle and the pedestrian are in: dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'), with rel.occupies anchoring each road user in a governed region (kind st.travel_region). 'not in operation' is a head showing 'dark' or dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'); 'not in place' is no such head governing those regions. dev.governs is used for control, not for a position, as its exclusion requires.

'the driver of a vehicle' maps, as in the run's index, to the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions decided by the reading); 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Yielding the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another') is observed as the vehicle not reaching the pedestrian: no rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap') and the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) bounded as the standard below sets; as mapped in the run's index for 'shall yield the right-of-way'.

'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'crossing the highway within a crosswalk': the crosswalk (DEF-NRS-484A-065: 'That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway ... distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing') is st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'), marked or unmarked, so the definition's whole extent is kept; rel.occupies places the pedestrian's footprint in it.

By the section's own definition, a half of the highway is 'all traffic lanes ... designated for traffic traveling in one direction': the pedestrian's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a lane (st.lane) or a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway') whose designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') points with the vehicle's heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points'): the half on which the vehicle travels, or, while it turns, the half its heading has turned onto. kin.heading is read as the direction of travel of a vehicle driven forward; st.lane 'Not a stand-in for' a half of the roadway does not apply because the half is assembled from the lanes' designated directions, as the definition itself builds it.

The section's definition of 'half of the highway' ('all traffic lanes of a highway which are designated for traffic traveling in one direction', 'the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway') is carried by the lanes (st.lane) grouped by their designated direction (st.lane_direction) and by a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'), the atoms c3 and st2 read.

operationalizations.standard: slowing down or stopping if need be so to yield (the right-of-way's 'danger of a crash unless one grants precedence')
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves (speed above the halt tolerance), a predicted closest approach of the two centres within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance is a danger of a crash the driver has not yielded to; a vehicle at rest has slowed or stopped as need be

operationalizations.standard: approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a pedestrian in the crosswalk on a lane whose designated direction points against the vehicle's heading is in danger where the predicted closest approach of the two centres falls within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), not engaged by LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. Devices are not in place or not in operation: every traffic signal head (dev.traffic_signal) that governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies shows dark or is inoperative (dev.inoperative). There is a pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps a crosswalk (st.crosswalk), such that every pedestrian signal head governing a travel region p occupies shows dark, p is not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A or LVMC_11_30_060_B, and either (a) p's footprint overlaps a lane or one-way roadway whose designated direction (st.lane_direction) has a positive dot product with the subject's heading (kin.heading) — the subject's half — or (b) otherwise (p on the opposite half) the predicted closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).
obligation: For every such pedestrian p: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and where the subject's speed (kin.speed) is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, it is not the case that the closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'official' is read through the presence of the signal heads in the scene.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: No signal head governs the subject's lane; a pedestrian stands in an unmarked crosswalk on a lane whose direction matches the subject's heading, 15 m ahead; the subject moves at 10 m/s with a predicted closest approach of 0.5 m in 1.5 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene, but the subject is at rest (speed 0.0 m/s) before the crosswalk while the pedestrian crosses its half.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A traffic signal head governing the subject's lane shows circular_green: the devices are in operation.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: No signal head governs the subject's lane; a pedestrian near the crosswalk is on the predicted collision course, but whether its footprint overlaps the crosswalk is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No signal heads and no pedestrian anywhere in the scene: the duty is decided for the subject alone as not engaged.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian in the crosswalk on the opposite half, on a lane whose direction points against the subject's heading, with no predicted closest approach within the horizon.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hayward 1972; Swedish traffic conflict technique)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

segmentation.text: A pedestrian
shall not suddenly leave a curb or other place of safety and walk or run into the path of a vehicle
which is so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield.

elements.justification: 'A pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...').

Leaving 'a curb or other place of safety' is the pedestrian's footprint (rel.occupies) coming onto the roadway (st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') from a place pedestrians are safe from vehicles: the sidewalk the curb bounds (st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'), a safety zone (st.safety_zone, 'an area within the highway marked off for pedestrians only') or a median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider). st.sidewalk is not used for a crosswalk, as its exclusion requires; st.roadway is not used for the sidewalk. 'into the path of a vehicle': the vehicle is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; the pedestrian is in its path where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance). These primitives are 'Not a stand-in for' contact or danger alone; here they bound the path the vehicle will sweep, the clearance and horizon set by the reading, and the impossibility is decided by the standard.

operationalizations.standard: so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield
operationalizations.convention: stopping-distance model: the vehicle cannot yield where the time to the predicted closest approach (prim.closest_approach_time) is less than the driver's perception-reaction time plus the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) divided by twice the braking deceleration, written as a product (2·a·t_ca < 2·a·t_r + v); the deceleration is selected by the surface: icy or snow-covered (env.ice_or_snow), else wet (env.wet_road), else dry

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) that leaves a place of safety at this observation: its footprint overlaps a roadway (st.roadway) here, and at the previous observation it overlapped no roadway and overlapped a sidewalk, a safety zone or a median or divider. The duty does not apply where NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject, nor where LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2 is engaged for a vehicle v of the scene.
obligation: There is no vehicle v (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) such that the closest approach of the subject and v falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance) and 2·a·t < 2·a·p.driver_reaction_time + speed(v), where t is prim.closest_approach_time with horizon p.conflict_horizon, speed(v) is v's kin.speed, and a is p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_decel_wet where env.wet_road holds, else p.following_decel_dry. With no vehicle in the scene, compliant.

narrowings.why: 'suddenly' is read through the vehicle's closeness at the moment the pedestrian leaves the place of safety: a departure is sudden in the law's sense where the vehicle is already too close to yield; the pedestrian's own abruptness is not measured.
'other place of safety' is read only through the sidewalk the curb bounds, a safety zone and a median or dividing section.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's motion: whether the vehicle can stop, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry road. The pedestrian steps from the sidewalk onto the roadway while a car 12 m away moves toward it at 12 m/s; predicted closest approach 0.5 m in 1.0 s, below 1.5 s + 12/(2·6) s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps off while the car is 70 m away at 12 m/s: no closest approach within the horizon.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian stays on the sidewalk throughout.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car is 12 m away at 12 m/s on a collision course, but whether the pedestrian's footprint overlaps the roadway or the sidewalk is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps off the sidewalk with no vehicle in the scene: the duty binds the pedestrian alone and is met.

param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hayward 1972; Swedish traffic conflict technique)

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated,
pedestrians facing the signal
may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal
and must be given
the right-of-way
by the drivers of all vehicles.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}'); 'in place' is a head present in the scene. 'such signals' regulate the crossing of the roadway they control: dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ... roadway'), traffic including pedestrians (DEF-NRS-484A-285: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles'), ties the head to the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (kinds st.roadway, st.lane). dev.governs is not used as a position.
'the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated' is the head's state walk (dev.pedestrian_signal state 'walk').

'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'facing the signal': the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') lies ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along the direction its body points (kin.heading, 'direction the body points'), within a cone and a reach. dev.position is used as the head's location, not as the place of a stop line or crossing, which its exclusion names.

'may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal' identifies the pedestrians the right-of-way is owed to: those on the roadway the head governs (rel.occupies of a st.roadway or st.lane region that head governs), facing the head, so moving toward it across the way. The highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines') is crossed by traversing its roadway; the sidewalk the words of the sibling subparagraphs call a place of safety is no part of the crossing.

Giving the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another') is observed as the vehicle not reaching the pedestrian (no rel.contact) with its speed (kin.speed) bounded as the standard sets, as the index maps 'Yield'.
'the drivers of all vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence where the two approach 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves (speed above the halt tolerance), a predicted closest approach of the two centres within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance is a danger of a crash in which the vehicle has not granted precedence

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), not engaged by LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. There are a pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), a pedestrian signal head d showing walk, and a roadway or lane r governed by d (dev.governs), with p's footprint overlapping r (rel.occupies), p facing d, and p not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A or LVMC_11_30_060_B. p faces d where, with Δ the vector from p's kin.position to d's dev.position and h p's kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach².
obligation: For every such pedestrian p: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and where the subject's speed (kin.speed) is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, it is not the case that the closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'the drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion: the duty binds each vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian on the roadway faces a pedestrian head 12 m ahead that governs that roadway and shows walk; the subject turns toward the crossing at 8 m/s with a predicted closest approach of 0.8 m in 1.2 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene with the subject at rest before the crossing.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The faced head shows dont_walk_steady.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid, but the head's state is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The head shows walk but no pedestrian is in the scene: decided for the subject alone as not engaged.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hayward 1972; Swedish traffic conflict technique)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a pedestrian signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08 (pedestrian signal heads placed at the far end of the crossing, in the pedestrian's line of sight)

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a pedestrian signal head at which the head counts as the one across the crossing the pedestrian faces: a wide urban crossing (six lanes and a median, about 30 m) plus the head's set-back behind the far curb
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08; AASHTO Green Book urban cross-section widths

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer,
a pedestrian
may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal,
but must complete the crossing before the countdown timer gets to zero.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute when a timer is displayed'); 'such signals' regulate the crossing of the roadway they control, read through dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ... roadway'; traffic includes pedestrians, DEF-NRS-484A-285) on a roadway or lane (kinds st.roadway, st.lane).

'“Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

The pedestrian who proceeds across the highway under this indication is one whose footprint came onto the governed roadway or lane (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) while the head showed it, facing the head: the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head') ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach — the direction of the signal. dev.position is not used as a crossing or a stop line.

Completing the crossing is having left the roadway or lane crossed: the pedestrian's footprint no longer overlaps it (rel.occupies). The countdown timer gets to zero at the end of the flashing interval it times, where the head stops showing the flashing indication with a countdown and shows dont_walk_steady (dev.pedestrian_signal states dont_walk_flashing with countdown, then dont_walk_steady).

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, with no vehicle v of the scene engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. The judged observation is the countdown's end for a pedestrian head d governing (dev.governs) a roadway or lane r: d shows dont_walk_steady here and showed dont_walk_flashing with its countdown at the previous observation. The subject's latest entry onto r (the latest earlier observation at which its footprint came to overlap r, not overlapping it at the observation before; history bound: that entry, searched back without other limit) was made while d showed dont_walk_flashing with its countdown and the subject faced d, and d showed dont_walk_flashing with countdown at every observation from that entry to the previous one. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where the entry lies before the recording, applicability is unknown.
obligation: At the countdown's end the subject's footprint does not overlap r (rel.occupies): it has completed the crossing.

narrowings.why: the countdown's reaching zero is read as the head's change from the flashing indication with countdown to the steady indication, which ends the interval the timer counts; the timer's displayed number is not read.
'complete the crossing' is read as the pedestrian's footprint having left the roadway or lane governed by the head; a pedestrian on a median or safety zone between roadways has left it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The head governing roadway r shows dont_walk_flashing with countdown; the pedestrian steps onto r facing it, walks slowly, and is still on r when the head turns dont_walk_steady.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps onto r during the flashing countdown and is on the far sidewalk, off r, when the head turns dont_walk_steady.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian entered r while the head showed walk; at the countdown's end it is still on r (the steady-indication duty governs it, not this one).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps onto r and is on it later, but the head's state is not observed, so neither the countdown interval nor its end can be told.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the pedestrian already on r while the head shows dont_walk_flashing with countdown; the head turns dont_walk_steady while it is still on r; its entry onto r is not recorded.
scenarios.boundary: the pedestrian's entry onto r, which lies before the recording

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer,
a pedestrian
may not proceed to cross the highway,
but a pedestrian
who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1)
may continue to cross the highway
but must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone if one is provided or other place of safety before the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and steady.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute'). The signal that indicates to a pedestrian ('such signals') is the head that governs the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', traffic including pedestrians by DEF-NRS-484A-285; kinds st.roadway, st.lane) and that the pedestrian faces: the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head') ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is not used as a stop line or crossing.
'illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with no countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Proceeding to cross the highway is coming onto the roadway or lane the head governs: the pedestrian's footprint comes to overlap it (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane). The highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095) includes the sidewalk, but the sibling words 'must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone' place the sidewalk outside the crossing, so the crossing begins on the roadway.
'a pedestrian' (the one excepted) is the same admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Entering the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) borrows (1)'s words: 'While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'. It is the pedestrian's latest step from a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) onto a roadway or lane (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) made while a pedestrian head (dev.pedestrian_signal) governing that roadway or lane (dev.governs) showed walk and the pedestrian faced it (dev.position ahead of kin.position along kin.heading within the cone and reach).
Continuing to cross is not having returned to a sidewalk (rel.occupies of st.sidewalk) since that entry: the pedestrian is still in the crossing it began.

compositions.why: It borrows the circumstances of subparagraph (1)'s permission — the walk indication illuminated, the pedestrian facing the signal, proceeding across the highway in its direction — to qualify how the pedestrian entered. Subparagraph (1)'s rule is a duty on drivers to give the right-of-way; whether that duty applied to some vehicle, held, or was complied with says nothing of how this pedestrian entered, so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.
compositions.quote: While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, with no vehicle v of the scene engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. There are a pedestrian head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) showing dont_walk_flashing without its countdown attribute and a roadway or lane r governed by d (dev.governs), the subject faces d, and the subject's footprint did not overlap r at the previous observation. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Excepted: the subject is continuing a crossing it began lawfully under subparagraph (1) — its latest step from a sidewalk onto a roadway or lane was made while a pedestrian head governing that roadway or lane showed walk and the subject faced that head, and its footprint has overlapped no sidewalk since.
obligation: The subject's footprint does not overlap r at this observation: it has not proceeded onto the roadway.

narrowings.why: 'proceed to cross the highway' is read as the pedestrian's footprint coming onto the roadway or lane the faced head governs; walking on the sidewalk is not crossing.

Subparagraph (2)'s rule is the duty to complete the crossing before the countdown ends; lawful entry under (2) does not depend on that later duty being complied with (the entry precedes it), so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.
