segmentation.text: A person,
except when stopping, standing or parking where no parking is permitted,
shall not start a vehicle which is stopped, standing or parked on a highway
nor enter upon a highway
unless and until such movement can be made with safety.

elements.justification: 'A person' who enters upon a highway with a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the binder is the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same mapping as the index row 'A person'.

'stopping, standing or parking' (DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'; DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle'; DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle') together denote every halt, drv.motion.complete_halt, read at the observation before the entry. 'where no parking is permitted': an st.curb_zone of kind no_parking, no_stopping or fire_lane or a curb painted red that the footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), or an st.travel_region it occupies governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking, no_standing or no_stopping whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold); the posted or painted feature is the evidence (status reading).

'enter upon a highway' is the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') an st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines', DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way'), having overlapped no highway region at the previous observation. st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway: the words name the highway.

operationalizations.standard: such movement can be made with safety
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a movement is made with safety where, at its onset, no other road user's centre is predicted under constant velocities to come within the conflict centre clearance of the subject's centre within the time-to-collision horizon

applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation at which the subject enters upon a highway: it occupies an st.highway region here and occupied none at the previous observation; and the exception does not hold: at the previous observation the subject was not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) in a place where no parking is permitted -- an st.curb_zone of kind no_parking, no_stopping or fire_lane or whose curb colour is red, or an st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking, no_standing or no_stopping whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold).
obligation: At that observation no other road user of the scene, of any class (same excludes the subject), satisfies prim.closest_approach_within(subject, other; p.conflict_horizon) with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, other; p.conflict_horizon) at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Where one does, violated.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who enters upon a highway is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle, whoever or whatever controls it.

'where no parking is permitted' is read by the posted no-parking, no-standing or no-stopping sign whose conditions hold, or the marked or red-painted curb zone, the feature's presence being the evidence of the restriction.

'with safety' is read only as the absence, at the entry, of a predicted near-collision with another road user; 'unless and until' is read at the entry observation, the entry being withheld until then.

segmentation.text: A driver
shall not stop
or suddenly decrease the speed
of a vehicle
without first giving an appropriate signal
to the driver of any vehicle immediately to the rear.

elements.justification: 'A driver' is the relational role of DEF-NRS-484A-080, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the binder is the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same mapping as the index row 'a driver'.

'stop' is here a stopping the clause prohibits, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 applies ('when prohibited, any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'): the onset of drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'), the observation at which it holds and did not at the previous one. The definition's exclusion, which the concept does not make, is carried beside it: 'except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' -- a road user ahead in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') within p.queue_halt_gap of body gap (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies'); 'or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' -- the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.stop_sign, a dev.yield_sign, a dev.traffic_signal showing a red indication, a dev.railway_signal_or_gate flashing or with gate lowering or down, or a dev.human_direction of role police_officer indicating stop. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position; it reads which device controls the region occupied.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the subject's class.

The signal of a stop or a decrease of speed is the brake lamp ('brake lamps lit') or the arm signal (sig.hand_signal, 'meaning ... stop_or_slow'). sig.brake_lamp is not a stand-in for a halt or a deceleration, and is not used as one: the halt and the deceleration are read from kinematics, the lamp only as the signal other road users see. 'first' is read as shown at the onset of the halt or the deceleration or at some observation of the window of length p.stop_signal_lead_window behind it.

'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, read on the other road user; 'immediately to the rear' is that road user behind the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction') with the gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.rear_signal_reach. rel.surface_gap is not a stand-in for an order of arrival; the order is read from rel.ahead_behind_in_lane. 'the driver of' is read through that vehicle (agency); no perception by that driver is read.

operationalizations.standard: suddenly
operationalizations.convention: a decrease of speed is sudden where the longitudinal deceleration exceeds the comfortable deceleration most drivers use when braking for an expected stop

applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation E at which either (a) drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) holds and did not hold at the previous observation, and that halt is not excused under DEF-NRS-484A-260: no road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with rel.surface_gap at most p.queue_halt_gap, and the subject occupies no st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.stop_sign, a dev.yield_sign, a dev.traffic_signal showing circular_red, red_arrow or flashing_red, a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down, or a dev.human_direction of role police_officer indicating stop; or (b) the subject's kin.accel_longitudinal is at or below minus p.sudden_decel_min and was not at the previous observation; and at E some other road user of the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle is behind the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with rel.surface_gap at most p.rear_signal_reach.
obligation: At E, or at some observation of the time window of length p.stop_signal_lead_window behind E, the subject showed sig.brake_lamp lit or a sig.hand_signal meaning stop_or_slow. Otherwise violated.

narrowings.why: 'A driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle, whoever or whatever controls it.
'an appropriate signal' is read as the brake lamps lit or the stop-or-slow arm signal; 'first' as shown at the onset or within the lead window behind it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject car halts mid-block in its lane with no road user ahead and no device or officer governing its lane; a car is 15 m behind it in the same lane; the brake lamps are not lit and no arm signal is given at any observation of the lead window or at the halt.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject car halts mid-block with a car 15 m behind in the same lane; its brake lamps are lit from 2 s before the halt.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car halts mid-block without any signal; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car halts mid-block with a car 15 m behind in the same lane; no arm signal is given, and sig.brake_lamp is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject car halts in a lane governed by a stop sign, with a car 15 m behind, without any signal: the halt is excused under DEF-NRS-484A-260 and the deceleration stays below the sudden threshold.

param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracking sources

param_proposals.source: AASHTO perception-reaction time of an alert driver to an expected cue (about 1.5 s)

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing any vehicle,
whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.

This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' (DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way'); rel.occupies anchors the subject on it. Same mapping as the index row 'on any highway'.

'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate. 'stop, park or leave standing' together denote every halt: DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not', DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not', DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle'; their exclusions (a halt to avoid conflict or on a device's direction; one receiving or discharging passengers; one loading) intersect only on purposes no conduct shows, so the union is drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation') with p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'no person' is read through the vehicle's conduct (agency).

st.roadway is 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder': the paved or main-traveled part. The roadway is not a stand-in for the sidewalk, and 'not on the roadway' includes the shoulder, which is the place off that part the words contrast it with. rel.occupies anchors the subject's footprint on it.

Nearest atoms only, shown to mark the gap: kin.engine_running is 'not a stand-in for motion or a halt' and an engine stopped does not make a vehicle unable to move; sig.hazard is a signal a road user emits, not the condition of the vehicle. Neither denotes a vehicle disabled so that it is impossible to avoid stopping; the span is filed as an atom gap.

operationalizations.standard: practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway
operationalizations.convention: leaving a vehicle off the main-traveled part is practicable where a shoulder or a parking bay lies on the same way within the distance a vehicle covers when braking from a rural speed at a comfortable deceleration

residues.why: The duty is the same whether or not a person is with the vehicle: the words say so expressly.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation where the subject occupies an st.highway region, the reading does not declare asm.business_or_residence_district for its place (declared false), the subject occupies an st.roadway region, and an st.shoulder or st.parking_space region lies on the same highway (st.on_way) within ground distance (st.region_geometry) p.offroad_refuge_reach of the subject's body. Not engaged where the subject is disabled so that it is impossible to avoid stopping (gap).
obligation: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) does not hold: the subject is not at rest on the roadway. A halt there is violated.

narrowings.why: 'no person shall stop, park or leave standing' is read through the vehicle's conduct, whoever controls it.
'practicable' is read as the presence of a shoulder or bay on the same way within the reach; whether that place is occupied or wide enough is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: District declared false; the subject car halts in the roadway lane of a rural highway for 60 s while a paved shoulder lies on the same way 2 m from its body.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: District declared false; the subject car drives along the roadway beside the shoulder at 20 m/s without halting.

scenarios.name: idle

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing any vehicle,
whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.

This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' (DEF-NRS-484A-095); rel.occupies anchors the subject on it. Same mapping as the index row 'on any highway'.
st.roadway is 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder': the paved or main-traveled part; rel.occupies anchors the subject's footprint on it.

'a standing vehicle' is the subject (admitted aggregate) at rest, drv.motion.complete_halt (DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not'). 'an unobstructed width of the highway opposite' is the free width across the roadway beside its body: prim.region_lateral_offset ('the signed lateral offset ... of a structure region from a road user') to the st.road_edge ('curb or edge of the roadway') on the same way (st.on_way) on the side away from the curb it stands at, less half its width (kin.extent, 'a formula reads the full length, width and height'), with no st.obstruction region and no halted other road user (rel.occupies of the roadway) within that width beside it (st.region_geometry). operationalizations.standard: the free passage of other vehicles
operationalizations.convention: a width is left for free passage where the unobstructed lateral width of roadway beside the standing vehicle is at least the width one passing design vehicle needs with its lateral clearance, about a narrow traffic lane

residues.why: The duty is the same whether or not a person is with the vehicle: the words say so expressly.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle. obligation: The lateral width from the subject's body to the st.road_edge region on the same way on its open side (prim.region_lateral_offset, less half the subject's width from kin.extent) is at least p.free_passage_width, and no st.obstruction region and no other halted road user lies within that width beside the subject. segmentation.text: A person
shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict
with other traffic
or in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer
or official traffic-control device,
in any of the following places:
Within 30 feet upon the approach to any official traffic-control signal
located at the side of a highway.

elements.justification: The words name the person who stops, stands or parks "a vehicle". Who controls a vehicle is not observable; the ontology reads the one who drives through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the road user judged is the vehicle (agency reading, disclosed). ru.aggregate is "membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id"; the admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle counts "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", its exceptions classified by the run's reading. Not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom (the words name none), nor for the relational role of who controls the vehicle: the atom states the class of the road user whose halts are judged.

"stop" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-260); "stand" is "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" other than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250); "park" is "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-155). Each is a halting, so forbidding all three forbids every halt of the vehicle at the place, however brief. drv.motion.complete_halt denotes that "The road user is at rest at the observation", observed as kin.speed at or below a tolerance, at each observation; what it does not denote ("a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance") is no halting. "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway").

"traffic" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"); "other" leaves out the subject itself. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ("a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction") places that traffic in the subject's path, and rel.surface_gap ("distance between the nearest points of two bodies") is the clearance to it that the operationalization of "necessary" bounds. Neither contract carries a not-a-stand-in clause this use touches; no centre distance and no order of arrival is read.

"in compliance with law" excuses a halt the law itself requires of the vehicle where it is. Observably those are the halt a stop sign requires (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt") and the halt a traffic signal requires while it shows a red indication (dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head" with states circular_red, red_arrow(dir) and flashing_red), each on the traffic of a travel region the device governs (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") that the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"; st.travel_region is the kind that relation ranges over here). dev.governs is "Not a stand-in for: a position — the region a device governs is not where a halt is required": the governed region is not read as the place of a required halt; it reads only that a vehicle within the governed approach, while the device commands a halt, is held there in obedience to it.

dev.human_direction is "a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}". A police officer ("every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic", DEF-NRS-484A-180) is the role police_officer, and the direction a halt complies with is the indication stop, given to the travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region the kind). dev.governs is not read as the place a halt is required, only as the traffic the direction is given to. A flagger or a crossing guard is another role and is not read.

An official traffic-control device is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The devices whose directions a halt obeys are a stop sign (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign: "regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt", whose yield may require a halt), a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), and a level-crossing signal with its lights flashing or its gate lowering or down (dev.railway_signal_or_gate: "lights ∈ {flashing, dark}; gate ∈ {up, lowering, down, raising, none}"), each governing the travel region the vehicle occupies (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region). "official" is the device's legal status, read from its presence. dev.governs is not read as the position of a required halt, only as the traffic the device directs; no sign is read as a manoeuvre.

A traffic-control signal is "any official traffic-control device, whether manually, electrically or mechanically operated, placed or erected by a public authority or railroad, by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed" (DEF-NRS-484A-290): the signal head dev.traffic_signal ("a signal head", states from circular_green to circular_red) is such a device. The law's words "upon the approach to" limit the signals to those whose controlled approach the vehicle is on, which leaves out a pedestrian signal (it directs pedestrians on a crossing, not an approach a vehicle stands on); "located at the side of a highway" leaves out the "overhead per-lane signal" dev.lane_control_signal; and a level-crossing signal (dev.railway_signal_or_gate) directs traffic to stop and never to proceed, so it is not one by which traffic is "alternately directed to stop or proceed". The approach is a travel region r the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) that the signal governs (dev.governs) or that enters (st.lane_enters: "the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end") an intersection (st.intersection) the signal governs, with the signal head (dev.position: "location of the device head / sign face") ahead of the vehicle's reference point (kin.position) along r's designated direction (st.lane_direction). "Within 30 feet" is the ground distance from the vehicle's front to the head: the distance from the reference point to the head less half the vehicle's length (kin.extent) at most the literal. dev.position is "Not a stand-in for: a stop line or a crossing": the words measure to the signal itself, which is the head. dev.governs is read only as which approach the signal controls; st.lane_enters is the source's entry record, never inferred from distance. "official" is read from the head's presence.

A highway is "the entire width between the boundary lines of every way" (DEF-NRS-484A-095), its sidewalks and shoulders included, so its side is the strip beyond the roadway's edge; a head over the roadway is not at its side. The head is located at the side where, in the vehicle's frame, its lateral offset (the component of the vector from kin.position to dev.position across kin.heading, left positive) lies farther to one side than a roadway edge on that side (st.road_edge: "curb or edge of the roadway"), whose signed offset is prim.region_lateral_offset ("the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user"). kin.heading is read only as the frame of the two offsets, not as a manoeuvre; dev.position is not read as a stop line or a crossing.

operationalizations.standard: necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
operationalizations.convention: queue spacing of halted vehicles: a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within that gap between bodies is a halt the traffic ahead makes necessary

applicability: The subject is a road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the observation there are a traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) and a travel region r whose footprint the subject's overlaps (rel.occupies) such that: d governs r, or r enters (st.lane_enters) an intersection that d governs (dev.governs); d's head (dev.position) lies ahead of the subject's reference point (kin.position) along r's designated direction (st.lane_direction: the dot product of the direction with the vector from the reference point to the head is positive); the squared ground distance from the subject's reference point to the head is at most the square of the literal 30 feet plus half the subject's length (kin.extent); and the head lies beyond a roadway edge: for some st.road_edge region e with signed lateral offset l from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset), the head's lateral offset in the subject's frame (the cross product of kin.heading with the vector from kin.position to dev.position, left positive) is at least l where l is positive, or at most l where l is negative.
obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds, the subject is not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), unless at that observation one of the exceptions holds: (a) some road user other than the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; (b) a stop sign, or a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); (c) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs a travel region the subject occupies; (d) a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down governs a travel region the subject occupies. Violated where the subject is at rest there and no exception holds.

narrowings.why: The person who stops the vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the rule judges the vehicle's halts whoever or whatever controls it.

"necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic" is read only as a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within the queue gap; a halt to let crossing or oncoming traffic clear, with nothing ahead in the lane, is not read as necessary, so such a halt is judged without this exception.
"official" is the device's legal status, read from the device's presence in the scene.
"official" said of the traffic-control signal is its legal status, read from the signal head's presence in the scene.

segmentation.text: A person
shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict
with other traffic
or in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer
or official traffic-control device,
in any of the following places:
Within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad.

elements.justification: The words name the person who stops, stands or parks "a vehicle". Who controls a vehicle is not observable; the ontology reads the one who drives through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the road user judged is the vehicle (agency reading, disclosed). ru.aggregate is "membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id"; the admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle counts "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", its exceptions classified by the run's reading. Not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom (the words name none), nor for the relational role of who controls the vehicle: the atom states the class of the road user whose halts are judged.

"stop" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-260); "stand" is "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" other than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250); "park" is "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-155). Each is a halting, so forbidding all three forbids every halt of the vehicle at the place, however brief. drv.motion.complete_halt denotes that "The road user is at rest at the observation", observed as kin.speed at or below a tolerance, at each observation; what it does not denote ("a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance") is no halting. "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway").

"traffic" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"); "other" leaves out the subject itself. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ("a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction") places that traffic in the subject's path, and rel.surface_gap ("distance between the nearest points of two bodies") is the clearance to it that the operationalization of "necessary" bounds. Neither contract carries a not-a-stand-in clause this use touches; no centre distance and no order of arrival is read.

"in compliance with law" excuses a halt the law itself requires of the vehicle where it is. Observably those are the halt a stop sign requires (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt") and the halt a traffic signal requires while it shows a red indication (dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head" with states circular_red, red_arrow(dir) and flashing_red), each on the traffic of a travel region the device governs (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") that the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"; st.travel_region is the kind that relation ranges over here). dev.governs is "Not a stand-in for: a position — the region a device governs is not where a halt is required": the governed region is not read as the place of a required halt; it reads only that a vehicle within the governed approach, while the device commands a halt, is held there in obedience to it.

dev.human_direction is "a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}". A police officer ("every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic", DEF-NRS-484A-180) is the role police_officer, and the direction a halt complies with is the indication stop, given to the travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region the kind). dev.governs is not read as the place a halt is required, only as the traffic the direction is given to. A flagger or a crossing guard is another role and is not read.

An official traffic-control device is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The devices whose directions a halt obeys are a stop sign (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign: "regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt", whose yield may require a halt), a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), and a level-crossing signal with its lights flashing or its gate lowering or down (dev.railway_signal_or_gate: "lights ∈ {flashing, dark}; gate ∈ {up, lowering, down, raising, none}"), each governing the travel region the vehicle occupies (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region). "official" is the device's legal status, read from its presence. dev.governs is not read as the position of a required halt, only as the traffic the device directs; no sign is read as a manoeuvre.

A railroad is "a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails" (DEF-NRS-484A-200); its rails on a highway are those of a level crossing, st.railway_crossing: "level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail". Who controls a vehicle is not observable; the ontology reads the one who drives through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the road user judged is the vehicle (agency reading, disclosed). ru.aggregate is "membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id"; the admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle counts "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", its exceptions classified by the run's reading. Not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom (the words name none), nor for the relational role of who controls the vehicle: the atom states the class of the road user whose halts are judged.

"stop" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-260); "stand" is "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" other than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250); "park" is "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-155). Each is a halting; drv.motion.complete_halt denotes that "The road user is at rest at the observation", observed as kin.speed at or below a tolerance, at each observation; what it does not denote ("a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance") is no halting. Which of the three halts is forbidden at a place is the one the device there prohibits (next span). "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway").

"traffic" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"); "other" leaves out the subject itself. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ("a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction") places that traffic in the subject's path, and rel.surface_gap ("distance between the nearest points of two bodies") is the clearance to it that the operationalization of "necessary" bounds. Neither contract carries a not-a-stand-in clause this use touches; no centre distance and no order of arrival is read.

"in compliance with law" excuses a halt the law itself requires of the vehicle where it is. Observably those are the halt a stop sign requires (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt") and the halt a traffic signal requires while it shows a red indication (dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head" with states circular_red, red_arrow(dir) and flashing_red), each on the traffic of a travel region the device governs (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") that the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"; st.travel_region is the kind that relation ranges over here). dev.governs is "Not a stand-in for: a position — the region a device governs is not where a halt is required": the governed region is not read as the place of a required halt; it reads only that a vehicle within the governed approach, while the device commands a halt, is held there in obedience to it.

dev.human_direction is "a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}". A police officer ("every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic", DEF-NRS-484A-180) is the role police_officer, and the direction a halt complies with is the indication stop, given to the travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region the kind). dev.governs is not read as the place a halt is required, only as the traffic the direction is given to. A flagger or a crossing guard is another role and is not read.

An official traffic-control device is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The devices whose directions a halt obeys are a stop sign (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign: "regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt", whose yield may require a halt), a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), and a level-crossing signal with its lights flashing or its gate lowering or down (dev.railway_signal_or_gate: "lights ∈ {flashing, dark}; gate ∈ {up, lowering, down, raising, none}"), each governing the travel region the vehicle occupies (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region). "official" is the device's legal status, read from its presence. dev.governs is not read as the position of a required halt, only as the traffic the device directs; no sign is read as a manoeuvre.

An official traffic-control device is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The devices that prohibit stopping, standing or parking are the point regulations dev.regulatory_sign of code no_stopping, no_standing or no_parking ("a point regulation by catalogue code"), in effect for the vehicle where their stated conditions hold at the observation (prim.conditions_hold: "the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user"), governing a travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region); and the marked or signed lengths of curb st.curb_zone of kind no_stopping or no_parking ("a signed or marked length of curb") that the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies). Each prohibition reads the halt it names: "stopping" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily" (DEF-NRS-484A-260), drv.motion.complete_halt; "standing" is "the halting of a vehicle" otherwise than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and "parking" "the standing of a vehicle" otherwise than temporarily while loading or unloading (DEF-NRS-484A-155), each read through how long the vehicle has been at rest, drv.motion.parked ("at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration"), with p.standing_min_duration and p.parking_min_duration. dev.regulatory_sign is "Not a stand-in for: a manoeuvre or a road feature — a prohibition sign is a condition": it is read as exactly that condition. dev.governs is read as the traffic the sign regulates, not as a halt position.

operationalizations.standard: necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
operationalizations.convention: queue spacing of halted vehicles: a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within that gap between bodies is a halt the traffic ahead makes necessary

applicability: The subject is a road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the observation either a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_stopping, no_standing or no_parking whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold) governs (dev.governs) a travel region whose footprint the subject's overlaps (rel.occupies), or the subject's footprint overlaps a st.curb_zone of kind no_stopping or no_parking.
obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds, the subject is not engaged in the conduct a device there prohibits: where a no_stopping sign or curb zone applies, the subject is not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance); where a no_standing sign applies, it is not standing (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance and p.standing_min_duration); where a no_parking sign or curb zone applies, it is not parked (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance and p.parking_min_duration); unless at that observation one of the exceptions holds: (a) some road user other than the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; (b) a stop sign, or a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); (c) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs a travel region the subject occupies; (d) a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down governs a travel region the subject occupies. Violated where the subject engages in a prohibited halt there and no exception holds.

narrowings.why: The person who stops the vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the rule judges the vehicle's halts whoever or whatever controls it.

"necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic" is read only as a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within the queue gap; a halt to let crossing or oncoming traffic clear, with nothing ahead in the lane, is not read as necessary, so such a halt is judged without this exception.
"official" is the device's legal status, read from the device's presence in the scene.
"official" said of the prohibiting devices is their legal status, read from the sign's or the marked curb's presence in the scene.

Standing and parking are told from a halt by their purpose (receiving or discharging passengers, temporary loading or unloading), which is not observable; the purpose is read through how long the vehicle has been at rest.

The prohibition is read respectively to the place: where a device prohibits stopping, any halt is forbidden; where it prohibits standing, standing; where it prohibits parking, parking. A brief halt where a device prohibits only parking is not read as forbidden, since the device there permits it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking with empty conditions governs the lane the subject, a ru.aggregate vehicle, occupies; the subject has been at rest (kin.speed zero) for 300 s; no other road user, no human direction and no other device is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the subject has been at rest for 20 s after moving, a halt shorter than parking.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is at rest in a lane that no prohibiting sign governs and overlaps no curb zone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe the subject's speed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A dev.regulatory_sign of code no_stopping with empty conditions governs the subject's lane; the subject halts for 2 s.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint overlaps a st.curb_zone of kind no_parking and it has been at rest for 400 s.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the sign's conditions state a time window that env.civil_time at the observation lies outside, so prim.conditions_hold is false.

scenarios.name: branch_4

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in this section [(2) and (3) appended below],
every vehicle
stopped or parked
upon a highway
where there are adjacent curbs
must be stopped or parked with the right-hand wheels of the vehicle parallel to and within 18 inches of the right-hand curb.
Local authorities may by ordinance permit parking
of vehicles with the left-hand wheels adjacent to and within 18 inches of the left-hand curb of a one-way highway.

Local authorities may by ordinance permit angle parking on any highway, except that angle parking must not be permitted on any highway constructed and maintained by the Department of Transportation under the authority granted by chapter 408 of NRS unless the Department has determined that the highway is of sufficient width to permit angle parking without interfering with the free movement of traffic.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Its exclusion (not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom, or for a role) does not apply: the words name the defined aggregate itself.

'stopped or parked' is a vehicle brought to rest: drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation ... observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance' (a parked vehicle is at rest too, so the halt covers both words). The section regulates the position of a vehicle at rest at the side of the way, so a halt in the stream of traffic is not the stop it speaks of (the stopping definition DEF-NRS-484A-260 itself leaves out a halt 'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'). That halt is read through the conduct it names: the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given'), or it has a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the queue spacing. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: it is read only as the control of the region the subject occupies. complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that.

'highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority') is st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; 'upon' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway: the words name the whole way, as the atom does.

A highway 'where there are adjacent curbs' is one along which a curb runs: st.lane_marking gives 'per side of a lane: type ∈ {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}', so a lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on the subject's highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') with a side of type curb shows the curbs. st.road_edge is not used for presence: its contract is 'curb or edge of the roadway' and does not tell a curb from an uncurbed edge. st.lane is not a stand-in for a lateral position here: it is read only for its side marking.

'parallel to ... the right-hand curb' with the right-hand wheels at it is a vehicle whose heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') lies along the designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') of the travel region it occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), within a parallelism tolerance, pointed with that direction (the right-hand curb is the curb on the right of the direction of travel, so its right side faces it only when headed with it). 'the right-hand curb' is a road edge (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway'; the highway's curbs are established by s5) lying on the same highway (st.on_way) on the vehicle's right: prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', below zero. 'within 18 inches' is the ground distance from the body outline to it (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)') at most the stated figure. st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy (it is read as a distance only); the lateral offset is read only for the side.

The permitted alternative position: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'a one-way highway' is the subject occupying (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'); 'the left-hand wheels adjacent to ... the left-hand curb' is the heading (kin.heading) along the roadway's designated direction (st.lane_direction) within the same parallelism tolerance, with a road edge (st.road_edge) on the same way (st.on_way) on the vehicle's left (prim.region_lateral_offset above zero); 'within 18 inches' is the body-to-edge ground distance (st.region_geometry) at most the stated figure. 'adjacent' is read as alongside, parallel to the curb, the same position as subsection 1 states for the right.

Angle parking permitted by the local authority shows on the road as an official traffic-control device: dev.regulatory_sign code 'angle_parking' governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), its 'structured conditions' holding (prim.conditions_hold), or a marked bay (st.parking_space, 'marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute') whose angle stands clear of zero by the source's angle resolution. The presence of the device is the evidence of the permission and of its lawfulness, including the Department's determination for a highway it maintains (status reading): the words that limit where the authority may permit angle parking bind the authority, not the road user. A sign is not a stand-in for a manoeuvre: it is read only as the permission of the place.

assumptions.meaning: the one-way way at the place of the road user at the observation is one on which the local authority having jurisdiction permits vehicles to park with their left-hand wheels at the left-hand curb, as the map's reading records

residues.why: The provisions the words point to are subsections (2) and (3), which are segments s7-s9 of this same text and are carried there as the exceptions of this node; the words add nothing beyond them, so the duty is the same whether or not they are read.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), is at rest at the observation (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance); it occupies (rel.occupies) a highway region h (st.highway) on which (st.on_way) some lane (st.lane) has a side whose marking type is curb (st.lane_marking); and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic: it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no road user of the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap.
obligation: At that observation, with h re-bound as in the applicability (a highway the subject occupies on which a lane has a curb-marked side), one of three holds; otherwise the duty is violated. (1) Right-hand curb: the subject occupies a travel region r lying on h whose designated direction d (st.lane_direction) has a dot product with the subject's heading (kin.heading) at or above p.parked_heading_cos, and some road edge region e (st.road_edge) lying on h (st.on_way) is on the subject's right (prim.region_lateral_offset of e below zero) at a ground distance from its body (st.region_geometry) of at most 18 inches (literal). (2) Left-hand curb of a one-way highway, where asm.left_curb_parking_permitted holds: the subject occupies a one-way roadway r (st.one_way_roadway) lying on h with heading·d at or above p.parked_heading_cos, and some road edge e lying on h is on its left (offset above zero) within 18 inches of its body. (3) Angle parking permitted: the subject occupies a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a regulatory sign of code angle_parking whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold), or it occupies a parking space (st.parking_space) whose angle exceeds p.parking_space_angle_resolution.

narrowings.why: The wheels are not observed: the body outline stands for them. The wheels lie inside the footprint, so the body-to-curb distance is at most the wheel-to-curb distance and the reading is lenient by the wheels' inset (a few centimetres). 'parallel' is read within the tolerance p.parked_heading_cos, headed with the designated direction, since the right-hand wheels face the right-hand curb only so.

Why a vehicle is stopped is not observed. The words speak of a vehicle stopped or parked to stand by the way (the stopping definition DEF-NRS-484A-260 itself leaves out a halt 'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'); a halt made for traffic is read through the conduct that shows it: a halt in a region a signal, sign, railway device or person directing traffic governs, or a halt queued behind a member of traffic within the queue spacing. A halt mid-way through a parking manoeuvre is judged like any other halt.

The permission given by ordinance, and its validity on a highway the Department maintains, is read from the posted angle-parking sign or the angled bay marking: the presence of the device presumes the status.
The duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

segmentation.text: Upon those highways which have official traffic-control devices permitting angle parking,
a person
shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle other than at the angle to the curb or edge of the highway indicated by such devices.

elements.justification: 'official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-145: 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority') 'permitting angle parking' is a regulatory sign of code 'angle_parking' (dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code') whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold) governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), or a marked angle bay (st.parking_space, 'marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute') the subject occupies whose angle stands clear of zero by the source's resolution. 'those highways' (st.highway) is read as the part of the way the device governs or marks, where the angle it indicates is defined. A sign is not a stand-in for a manoeuvre: it is read as the permission of the place.

'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stops, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. Who controls the vehicle is read through its controlled motion.

'stop' prohibited takes DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155) are halts as well, so the three verbs are read as the halting they all are. Halting is drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or another road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap). complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that. 'other than at the angle ... indicated by such devices' maps to its nearest atoms: kin.heading, st.lane_direction, st.parking_space, st.road_edge (see the gap). The angle at which the vehicle meets the curb has as its cosine the dot product of its heading (kin.heading) with the designated direction (st.lane_direction) of the curb-side travel region; the angle the devices indicate is the bay's 'angle attribute' (st.parking_space), a number of degrees; the curb or edge is st.road_edge. No operator of the formula language relates a cosine to an angle given in degrees (Term has add, sub, mul, div, neg, abs and cond only), so whether the vehicle stands at the indicated angle cannot be written: see the operator gap.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a regulatory sign of code angle_parking whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold), or occupies a parking space (st.parking_space) whose angle exceeds p.parking_space_angle_resolution.
obligation: Violated where the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance), its halt is not one in the stream of traffic (it occupies no travel region governed by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or person directing traffic, and no road user is ahead of it in its lane within p.queue_halt_gap between bodies), and it does not stand at the angle the device indicates: it occupies a parking space p of angle θ (st.parking_space) and the dot product of its heading (kin.heading) with the designated direction d (st.lane_direction) of the travel region on the same way nearest p differs from the cosine of θ by more than p.bay_angle_cos_tolerance. Where the subject is in a sign-governed region with no bay, the indicated angle is unobserved and the verdict of a non-traffic halt is unknown. The comparison of a cosine with θ needs the operator of the gap.

narrowings.why: The three verbs are read as the halting they all are, with the stopping definition's exception (traffic conflict, a device's or an officer's direction) read through the device the subject's region is governed by and a queue ahead within the queue spacing; standing's and parking's own exceptions (passengers, loading) are within that halting and add no further excuse.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

gaps.proposal: Term.cosDeg (a : Term) : the cosine of an angle a given in degrees, a ratio; unknown where a is unknown. It decides where the act is required: whether a vehicle stands at the angle the devices indicate, by comparing the cosine of its angle to the curb (the dot product of kin.heading with the curb-side carrier's st.lane_direction) with the cosine of the bay's angle (st.parking_space angle, deg).
gaps.nearest: kin.heading and st.lane_direction give the cosine of the vehicle's angle to the curb; st.parking_space gives the indicated angle in degrees; no Term relates the two (no trigonometric operator), and an approximation by a table of literal angles would be a model the words do not state.

segmentation.text: Whenever lights are displayed upon
a vehicle
lawfully
parked
at nighttime
upon any highway,
such lights shall be depressed or dimmed,
in the event cowl or parking lamps are not used.

elements.justification: 'lights are displayed' is a lamp of the vehicle lit: sig.headlamp 'state ∈ {off, low_beam, high_beam}' not off, or sig.position_lamp 'position, parking, cowl or tail lamps lit'. Neither is a stand-in for anything the contracts exclude; they are lamps lit.

'vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320 ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

Nearest atoms only: a posted parking prohibition (dev.regulatory_sign governing, dev.governs, the travel region the vehicle occupies) is one ground of unlawful parking among many; 'lawfully parked' is the verdict of every parking rule the vehicle's standing engages, which no atom carries and Formula.rule cannot compose, since the words name no rule. See the operator gap.

'parked' is DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading', which drv.motion.parked denotes: at rest at every observation of the window behind of length min_duration, a shorter halt being the temporary one the definition leaves out.
'nighttime' is env.darkness, 'insufficient natural light; the boundary relative to sunset and sunrise is a reading parameter': the reading fixes the boundary, the atom carries the state.

'upon any highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way') is rel.occupies of st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; not the roadway alone.
'depressed or dimmed' is the headlamp beam lowered: sig.headlamp state low_beam (or off), never high_beam.

'cowl or parking lamps are not used' is the case in which the lights displayed are the headlamps rather than the cowl or parking lamps alone: sig.headlamp not off. sig.position_lamp cannot carry it: tail and position lamps are lit with the headlamps as well, so their being lit does not tell parking lamps used in place of headlamps.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, is parked (drv.motion.parked, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration p.parking_min_duration), occupies (rel.occupies) a highway (st.highway), in darkness (env.darkness), with a lamp lit (sig.headlamp not off, or sig.position_lamp), its headlamps being lit (sig.headlamp not off), and its parking is lawful (every parking rule it engages complied with: the operator of the gap).
obligation: The subject's headlamp state (sig.headlamp) is not high_beam.

gaps.proposal: Formula.compliesWithEngaged (who : Arg) (conduct : String) : at the observation, every rule of the set that governs conduct of the named kind (here standing or parking) and is engaged for road user who is complied with. It decides which road users the duty concerns: a vehicle lawfully parked, as against one parked against any parking rule (the same need as gap smoke31-1111-0039:G22 for 'in compliance with law').
gaps.nearest: dev.regulatory_sign, dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region: a posted prohibition governing the vehicle's place is one ground of unlawful parking among many (distances from hydrants, crosswalks, curbs; durations), so its absence is not lawfulness; Formula.rule composes one named rule only, and the words name none.

segmentation.text: Unless otherwise provided by ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction,
a person
shall not: Stop, stand or park a vehicle
within an alley
in a business district
except for the expeditious loading or unloading of goods.

elements.justification: 'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stops, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. Who controls the vehicle is read through its controlled motion.

'Stop' prohibited takes DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155) are halts as well, so the three verbs are read as the halting they all are. Halting is drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or another road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap). complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that.

'alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015: a highway 'Within a city block set apart for public use', 'Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; 'within' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... alley ...)'.

operationalizations.standard: expeditious loading or unloading of goods
operationalizations.convention: Loading or unloading is a purpose, read through the conduct it explains; 'expeditious' bounds how long that conduct may keep the vehicle standing. A halt counts as the expeditious loading or unloading the words except while the vehicle has not been at rest for longer than the temporary-halt bound of a loading zone (p.parking_min_duration): drv.motion.parked, at rest at every observation of that window behind, marks a halt beyond it.

assumptions.meaning: the alley at the place of the road user at the observation is one on which an ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction regulates stopping, standing or parking by provisions of its own, as the map's reading records

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) an alley region (st.alley); asm.business_district holds at its place; and asm.local_alley_ordinance does not hold (where it holds the duty does not arise).
obligation: Violated where the subject is parked (drv.motion.parked with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.parking_min_duration: at rest at every observation of the window behind, so beyond an expeditious halt for loading or unloading) and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic: it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap. Compliant otherwise.

narrowings.why: The three verbs are read as the halting they all are, with the stopping definition's exception read through the device the subject's region is governed by and a queue ahead within the queue spacing; standing's and parking's own exceptions add no further excuse.
The purpose of the halt is not observed: any halt no longer than the temporary-halt bound is read as the excepted loading or unloading, and a longer one as not excepted, whatever the vehicle does.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

segmentation.text: Unless otherwise provided by ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction,
a person
shall not: Stop, stand or park a vehicle
in any other
alley
in such a manner, or under such conditions as to leave available less than 10 feet of the width of the alley for the free movement of vehicular traffic.

elements.justification: 'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stops, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'Stop' prohibited takes DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; standing and parking are halts as well, so the three verbs are read as the halting they all are: drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap).

'alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015: a highway 'Within a city block set apart for public use', 'Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; the vehicle in it is rel.occupies.

The width of the alley left available beside the halted vehicle is measured on each side from its body: to the alley's edge, a road edge region (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway') on that side (prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive)', read for its sign only) at the ground distance from the body (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'); 'under such conditions' covers what else narrows that width beside it: an obstruction (st.obstruction, 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user') on that side within the width, or a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt) alongside (rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'the length the two footprints' projections ... share', at or above zero) on that side (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame') with a lateral gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, lateral component) inside it. The width available is the free width on one side, never the two sides added, since a vehicle moves past on one side. 'the free movement of vehicular traffic' (traffic of vehicles, DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) names whom the width serves: the duty binds whether or not a vehicle is present to use it. The region distance is not a stand-in for occupancy; the bearing and overlap are not a contact or distance and are read only for side and alongside.

assumptions.meaning: the alley at the place of the road user at the observation is one on which an ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction regulates stopping, standing or parking by provisions of its own, as the map's reading records

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) an alley region (st.alley); asm.business_district does not hold at its place ('any other' alley: one not in a business district, the alleys of paragraph (a) being those in one); asm.local_alley_ordinance does not hold; and its position leaves less than 10 feet (literal) of the alley's width free on either side: a side (left: prim.region_lateral_offset above zero, rel.bearing lateral component positive; right: below zero, negative) is free where some road edge region (st.road_edge) lies on that side, every road edge region on that side lies at a ground distance from the subject's body (st.region_geometry) of at least 10 feet, every obstruction (st.obstruction) on that side lies at least 10 feet from the body, and every other road user of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt) alongside the subject (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) on that side has a lateral gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, lateral) of at least 10 feet; the condition holds where neither side is free.
obligation: The subject does not halt there: violated where it is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic (it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap); compliant otherwise.

narrowings.why: The three verbs are read as the halting they all are, with the stopping definition's exception read through the device the subject's region is governed by and a queue ahead within the queue spacing.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

segmentation.text: A person
shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle
within an alley
in such position as to block the driveway or entrance to any abutting property.

elements.justification: 'A person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stops, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'stop' prohibited takes DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; standing and parking are halts as well: drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or another road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap).

'alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015: a highway 'Within a city block set apart for public use', 'Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; 'within' is rel.occupies.

Nearest atoms: blocking is the subject's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) the mouth of the entrance, or its body standing across it within a gap (st.region_geometry); 'driveway' is DEF-NRS-484A-190, 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel by the owner'. st.driveway_or_alley_entrance is 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway' and is 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there — the kind does not tell an alley's entrance from a private road's or driveway's': inside an alley it would equally mark the alley's own junction with the street, which is no entrance to abutting property. See the atom gap.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) an alley region (st.alley), and its position blocks the entrance to abutting property: its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the region where a driveway or other entrance to property meets the alley, or its body lies within p.entrance_block_gap of that region (st.region_geometry). Which regions are such entrances needs the atom of the gap.
obligation: The subject does not halt there: violated where it is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic (it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap); compliant otherwise.

narrowings.why: The three verbs are read as the halting they all are, with the stopping definition's exception read through the device the subject's region is governed by and a queue ahead within the queue spacing.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
